tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

Exit code 1
# Matrix handoff

Prepared by the matrix session (Claude) on 2026-09-25. This file acknowledges `HANDOFF-CODEX.md` and accepts its ownership split. The matrix session writes this file and everything under `matrix/`. It doesn't touch `runs/`, `builds/`, `reviews/` or `HANDOFF-CODEX.md`.

## Candidate

- Branch `push-pull-validation-head` at `b3796a70b526541014c92a40f685389060b862fe`, local only, in `/mnt/data/projects/discourse-graph/.claude/worktrees/push-pull-validation`.
- It is main `4a13294a` plus #1383 (ENG-2131), #1475 (ENG-2202), #1477 (ENG-2288), #1479 (ENG-2296) and #1482 (Obsidian import file names, external). It merged with no conflicts. #1412 was left out because it only adds tests and is based on a pre-merge branch.
- The candidate has no Supabase migrations. Its only `packages/database` change is converter code (`src/lib/crossAppConverters.ts`, +1 line).
- CI receipt: `matrix/receipts/ci-validate-b3796a70.log` records `pnpm ci:validate` passing on `b3796a70`, with 8/8 check-types and all unit suites (roam 62 files, obsidian 6, database 7, content-model 2, website).

## Files

| Path | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `matrix/cases.json` | Canonical cases. sha256 `27e594091fbf66f57db56636c0ba6ef92dcb1c0266d6687001d85599e7e1285e` |
| `matrix/push-pull-test-matrix.tsv` | One row per case and direction, in the bug-bash sheet's column order. sha256 `adf470313c555fb53511c462e64d0274e229e54211286eaa0b5b4b53283e97f5` |
| `matrix/push-pull-test-matrix.html` | Generated page. sha256 `e65c42c32019a1a7caab681e941e1af7463bd48068e830fe47634792b38a2ac1` |
| `matrix/template.html`, `matrix/build.mjs`, `matrix/check.mjs` | Generator: `node matrix/build.mjs` rebuilds the page and TSV from `cases.json`; `node matrix/check.mjs` checks the page script parses |
| `matrix/recon/*.md` | The six code-reader reports behind the ratings: roam-source, roam-destination, obsidian, database, linear-specs, github-context |

The published page is private to Sid: https://claude.ai/artifact/PPJhCiaXpp7LB7C11GRpTf. To update it, read that URL with the Artifact tool, then republish the rebuilt HTML with `url` set to it.

## Case schema

Each case in `cases.json` has these fields:

- `id`: stable across revisions.
- `area`: one of JRN, PUB, DSC, TXT, TTL, SRC, AST, UPD, DEL, REL, SCH, CNV, COL, RND, UX, SCL, SEC.
- `title`
- `dirs`: any of RR, RO, OR, OO, 3S (three spaces), DB (database).
- `steps`
- `expected`: the observable outcome, or "Not specified" for a product question.
- `src`: the ticket or document behind `expected`.
- `rating`:
  - `risk`: code reading suggests `expected` won't hold.
  - `decide`: needs a product decision.
  - `gap`: known or accepted for v0.
  - `pass`: expected to pass.
  - `unknown`
- `why`
- `ev`: code or PR references for the rating.
- `method`: `bash` (real-product bug bash), `db` (local database test) or `auto` (automated conversion test).
- `evidence`: what a pass records, `shot` (screenshot), `log` (assertion output or log) or `receipt` (written receipt). Failures always get the failure capture and, later, a video.
- `pri`: P0 to P2.
- `smoke`: set on the four journeys.
- `iso`: needs throwaway spaces.

Counts at this revision:

- 172 cases.
- Ratings: 43 risk, 22 decide, 21 gap, 56 pass, 30 unknown.
- Methods: 156 bash, 10 db, 6 auto.
- Journeys J-RR, J-RO, J-OR and J-OO are the smoke checks.

A rating is a code hypothesis, not a result. A `decide` row stays unresolved until an expected outcome is agreed.

## What the matrix session checked by hand

Everything else in `why` comes from the reader reports and cites code, but wasn't re-read by hand.

- **UPD-04.** `getImportedNodeUids` has no page restriction, so refresh-all also walks relation, schema and type blocks that carry `importedFrom` (`apps/roam/src/utils/importedSourceIdentity.ts:81-94`, `refreshAllImportedNodes.ts:13`).
- **DEL-04.** `loadRelations` returns an empty file on any read, parse or shape error (`apps/obsidian/src/utils/relationsStore.ts:35-62`), and orphan relation deletion then removes every synced relation concept (`apps/obsidian/src/utils/publishNode.ts:296-310`).
- **DEL-05.**
  - Confirmed: at load, `initializeSupabaseSync` runs `cleanupOrphanedNodes` (`apps/obsidian/src/utils/syncDgNodesToSupabase.ts:1133-1149`), which builds the local set from `metadataCache.getFileCache(file)?.frontmatter` (`apps/obsidian/src/utils/getDiscourseNodes.ts:18-52`).

# Independent review of the combined validation matrix

The 172-case matrix has useful breadth, but several steps and expectations need correction before it becomes the execution checklist. All 43 high-risk rows have an independent source review in `codex-high-risk-review.json`. These are code findings, not test results. No live application, database or security check was executed.

The matrix session remains the sole writer of the canonical cases. This report proposes changes for that session to incorporate.

## Reviewed inputs

- Candidate: `push-pull-validation-head`, `b3796a70b526541014c92a40f685389060b862fe`.
- Runtime source was read in Codex's worktree at `09d97321`. Its five-PR runtime merge has exactly the same Git tree as the candidate. The remaining changes are tests, test configuration and the prior inventory.
- Canonical matrix: `/mnt/data/projects/dg-validation-eng-1883/matrix/cases.json`. The scratchpad copy used during review has the same bytes.
- Matrix SHA-256: `27e594091fbf66f57db56636c0ba6ef92dcb1c0266d6687001d85599e7e1285e`.
- Frozen review input: `codex-input-cases-27e59409.json`. It is evidence for this review, not another canonical matrix.
- Verified inventory: 172 unique case IDs, 17 areas, 43 high risk, 22 needs a decision, 21 known gaps, 56 expected to pass and 30 unknown. The TSV contains 376 data rows with 16 columns each, matching the current direction expansion. Generic `3S` rows have not yet been expanded into concrete platform assignments.
- The private artifact URL could not be opened through the available web tool. The local JSON and TSV were read directly. The HTML page and Copy button were not tested.

Source references below are relative to the pinned runtime tree. The per-case JSON includes further references.

## Corrections before execution

1. **J-RR, J-RO, J-OR, J-OO: import the Claim before expecting its relation.** The journeys publish Source, Evidence and Claim, then import only Evidence and expect the Claim relation to be pending. Automatic Source import does not import the unrelated Claim endpoint. Roam discovery filters for both endpoints being local/imported (`apps/roam/src/utils/discoverSharedRelations.ts:88`); Obsidian relation import skips an unresolved endpoint (`apps/obsidian/src/utils/importRelations.ts:263`). First import Evidence and check Source inclusion. Then explicitly import Claim, check the pending relation and accept it. A later refresh of a deleted Claim also requires a Claim copy to exist locally. Wait for observed source sync/cleanup before destination refresh; elapsed time alone is not proof.

2. **SRC-03: the ordinary missing-Source behavior is already settled.** Sid's supplied meeting notes explicitly selected `[[@placeholder]]`. The current candidate implements it in `apps/roam/src/utils/sourceSlot.ts:15` and `apps/roam/src/utils/materializeSharedNode.ts:178`. Test placeholder plus warning for a Source-bearing type and core title. Keep the existing collision fallback as a separate fixture: if the synthesized placeholder title collides, the candidate retains the incoming title and warns (`materializeSharedNode.ts:184`). Older ticket prose does not require reopening the ordinary placeholder choice.

3. **PUB-07: remove the obsolete zero-success message claim.** `apps/roam/src/components/Export.tsx:899` now says `No nodes were published.` when there are no successes. Lines 931 onward use warning intent and leave the dialog open. Mixed-row and schema/relation failure accounting still deserve tests, but the old message is not evidence against this candidate.

4. **UPD-04: allow legitimate skipped nodes.** Refresh-all deliberately skips unchanged content (`apps/roam/src/utils/materializeSharedNode.ts:431`). The assertion should be no spurious failures and correct node-only totals. The broad import-marker query still supports the concern that schema pages and relation blocks enter the batch (`apps/roam/src/utils/importedSourceIdentity.ts:81`).

5. **SRC-04: distinguish remote availability from a local Source copy.** A forced refresh resolves a Source already present in the destination; it does not import a newly published Source (`apps/roam/src/utils/materializeSharedNode.ts:145`). To isolate the unchanged-timestamp problem, publish the Source, explicitly import it locally, then compare refresh-all with forced refresh on the unchanged Evidence. Keep automatic dependency import as a separate initial-import check.

6. **SRC-06, UPD-10 and UPD-11: avoid reloads while testing the failure cutoff.** The counter is module state and retries use exponential backoff (`apps/roam/src/utils/syncDgNodesToSupabase.ts:894`, `:1674`). Five reloads are not five consecutive failures in one loaded client. Use controlled failure injection/scheduler checks or observe the same loaded client. Distinguish error messages during a failed run from a message that future scheduling stopped. Roam's normal scheduling baseline is five minutes; Obsidian's edit debounce is five seconds. Neither is a completion guarantee.

7. **REL-15: correct the identifier explanation.** The visibility concern has source support, but the stored endpoint is a constructed RID, while `getRelationsForFile` looks for the bare local node ID or imported RID (`apps/obsidian/src/utils/relationsStore.ts:246`, `:441`). An original local note normally has no imported RID. Check both endpoint panels and the stored relation independently.

8. **UX-03 and UX-07: make the triggers sufficient.** UX-03 needs a relation-stage exception in addition to all selected node imports failing; missing endpoints can simply filter the relations out. UX-07 needs an uncached source name; restarting alone is insufficient because names are saved in settings (`apps/obsidian/src/components/ImportNodesModal.tsx:86`).

9. **DSC-10 and UX-06: distinguish error details from aggregate results.** Obsidian increments failed node counts when required type metadata is absent, and its modal reports that count. Calling the whole path console-only is inaccurate. Automatic Source imports are not included in the selected-root success count; decide whether that notice counts selections or every implicit write before treating the count as wrong. Missing asset feedback is a separate assertion.

10. **TXT-08: recheck its obsolete heading-removal premise.** The current Roam importer strips Obsidian frontmatter and trims blank lines, then passes the body through (`apps/roam/src/utils/materializeSharedNode.ts:223`). This path does not contain the claimed leading-title-heading removal. Keep a real first-heading fixture, but do not turn an old implementation detail into an unresolved product decision without fresh evidence.

# Per-case independent high-risk review

All 43 high-risk rows from matrix `27e59409` are reviewed below against runtime candidate `b3796a70`. These dispositions describe source evidence and test preparation, not execution results. No live application or database test was run.

See `codex-matrix-review.md` for the smoke-test corrections, settled placeholder expectation, coverage additions and backend decision. Canonical cases remain owned by the matrix session.

## PUB-05

Review: **supported path**

The title observer checks imported identity; the command, Export selection and node converter do not apply that guard. Reproduce through each entry point and verify origin identity of any new publication, not only whether a dialog opens.

Source: `apps/roam/src/utils/registerCommandPaletteCommands.ts:284`, `apps/roam/src/components/Export.tsx:243`, `apps/roam/src/utils/initializeObserversAndListeners.ts:127`, `apps/roam/src/utils/roamToCrossAppConverters.ts:133`.

## PUB-07

Review: **revise claim**

The old success-message claim is contradicted: zero success produces No nodes were published, warning intent, and no close. Retain mixed-row/dependency failure counting as a separate check.

Source: `apps/roam/src/components/Export.tsx:882`, `apps/roam/src/components/Export.tsx:899`, `apps/roam/src/components/Export.tsx:931`.

## PUB-09

Review: **qualify trigger**

Conversion writes nodeTypeId without ensuring nodeInstanceId; the group action rejects an absent instance ID before sync. Whether automatic file events have already supplied it is timing-dependent. Record frontmatter and test without an intervening edit or full sync.

Source: `apps/obsidian/src/utils/createNode.ts:212`, `apps/obsidian/src/utils/fileChangeListener.ts:164`, `apps/obsidian/src/utils/publishGroupSelection.ts:101`.

## PUB-10

Review: **supported path**

Enabling the setting starts an initial sync, but creates no file listener there. The listener is constructed only on plugin load. Assert initial sync separately from subsequent edit delivery.

Source: `apps/obsidian/src/index.ts:97`, `apps/obsidian/src/components/AdminPanelSettings.tsx:20`.

## DSC-10

Review: **revise claim**

Roam can continue without a resolved type. Obsidian missing-type metadata increments failedCount, which the modal reports in its aggregate notice; console-only is too broad. Distinguish a missing schema row from a schema-query error and inspect imported content plus visible feedback.

Source: `apps/roam/src/utils/resolveSharedNodeTypes.ts:69`, `apps/obsidian/src/utils/importNodes.ts:1242`, `apps/obsidian/src/utils/importNodes.ts:1699`, `apps/obsidian/src/components/ImportNodesModal.tsx:225`.

## TXT-02

Review: **qualify oracle**

The link rewriter does not implement arbitrary Roam syntax conversion. Keep block-boundary preservation and promised readable content as assertions; classify individual unsupported constructs against the v0 fidelity scope. A native macro and a markdown link are different fixtures.

Source: `apps/obsidian/src/utils/importNodes.ts:672`.

## TTL-04

Review: **supported path**

Roam sends template_content while Obsidian requires both parsed.templateContent and parsed.template to create a template file. Use a new destination type with Templates enabled and record the actual serialized schema.

Source: `apps/roam/src/utils/conceptConversion.ts:72`, `apps/obsidian/src/utils/importNodes.ts:1283`.

## TTL-06

Review: **supported path**

Roam node import matches names exactly; its relation-schema import folds case. Obsidian uses normalized labels. Use different schema IDs so ID matching does not mask the inconsistency.

Source: `apps/roam/src/utils/resolveSharedNodeTypes.ts:34`, `apps/roam/src/utils/importSharedRelations.ts:41`, `apps/obsidian/src/utils/schemaMatching.ts:28`.

## TTL-13

Review: **platform check needed**

The filename helper leaves CON unchanged. Native Windows create/rename behavior still needs a Windows run. Ensure the final decorated filename is actually CON.md, without a type prefix that changes the fixture.

Source: `apps/obsidian/src/utils/noteFileName.ts:9`, `apps/obsidian/src/utils/importNodes.ts:1729`.

## TTL-17

Review: **supported path**

Incremental concept upsert is gated on a title change, while imported Obsidian content can supply its own nodeTypeId. Keep the filename unchanged and inspect the persisted schema ID as well as both destination UIs.

Source: `apps/obsidian/src/utils/syncDgNodesToSupabase.ts:931`, `apps/obsidian/src/utils/importNodes.ts:1699`.

## SRC-04

Review: **revise steps**

An unchanged Evidence is skipped by refresh-all. Forced refresh resolves an already-local Source; it does not import a newly published Source. Split remote publication, local Source import, refresh-all and forced refresh into distinct steps.

Source: `apps/roam/src/utils/materializeSharedNode.ts:431`, `apps/roam/src/utils/materializeSharedNode.ts:145`, `apps/roam/src/utils/refreshImportedNode.ts:53`.

## SRC-05

Review: **qualify trigger**

The Source-slot extractor explicitly excludes @placeholder. The separate concern is classification/publication of the standalone @placeholder page by the Source node format. Test those separately; do not describe slot leakage as already established.

Source: `apps/roam/src/utils/sourceSlot.ts:15`, `apps/roam/src/utils/sourceSlot.ts:96`, `apps/roam/src/utils/initializeObserversAndListeners.ts:119`.

## SRC-06

Review: **local test needed**

The imported Source origin RID is reused and the SQL resolves it during concept conversion. Deletion versus revoked access may differ. Reproduce the exact DB error and result first. The retry cutoff must be observed within one loaded client, not by resetting it with reloads.

Source: `apps/roam/src/utils/sourceSlot.ts:107`, `packages/database/supabase/schemas/concept.sql:345`, `packages/database/supabase/schemas/concept.sql:432`, `apps/roam/src/utils/syncDgNodesToSupabase.ts:1674`.

## AST-04

Review: **supported path**

Obsidian rewrites wiki/markdown links and images, with no branch for a Roam pdf/audio/video macro URL. Record the published markdown for each media kind before attributing the outcome; successful download alone is insufficient.

Source: `apps/obsidian/src/utils/importNodes.ts:672`, `apps/obsidian/src/utils/importNodes.ts:728`.

## AST-15

Review: **supported path**

Binary-file changes are ignored by the edit listener and the picker blocks already-shared groups. Compare source bytes, FileReference hash, stored bytes and destination bytes; keep an explicit note edit/full-sync control separate.

Source: `apps/obsidian/src/utils/fileChangeListener.ts:86`, `apps/obsidian/src/components/PublishGroupSuggestModal.tsx:54`.

## AST-20

Review: **supported path**

The Roam asset rewriter scans the whole string without code-fence exclusion. Supply a real matching asset reference, since unmapped links are intentionally unchanged. Cover fenced and inline code separately.

Source: `apps/roam/src/utils/rewriteAssetLinks.ts:303`, `apps/roam/src/utils/rewriteAssetLinks.ts:420`, `apps/roam/src/utils/rewriteAssetLinks.ts:447`.

## UPD-04

Review: **revise oracle**

The broad import-marker query includes relation blocks and schema pages. The proposed N refreshed, 0 skipped oracle is wrong for unchanged nodes. Require zero spurious failures, correct node-only totals and legitimate skipped counts.

Source: `apps/roam/src/utils/importedSourceIdentity.ts:81`, `apps/roam/src/utils/refreshAllImportedNodes.ts:13`, `apps/roam/src/utils/materializeSharedNode.ts:431`.

## UPD-05

Review: **supported path**

A page with imported identity gets Refresh without a content-node check. Use a schema page actually created by relation import and verify the button action, not merely its presence.

Source: `apps/roam/src/utils/initializeObserversAndListeners.ts:125`, `apps/roam/src/utils/importSharedRelations.ts:68`.

## UPD-06

Review: **supported path**

Both DataCore and fallback imported-page enumeration are constrained to import/. Test moving a note with intact identity metadata using both query modes.

Source: `apps/obsidian/src/services/QueryEngine.ts:374`, `apps/obsidian/src/services/QueryEngine.ts:635`.

## UPD-10

Review: **qualify trigger**

The per-space title uniqueness constraint and upsert-before-cleanup order support a collision risk. Keep old and new UIDs distinct. Do not expect an existing imported copy to silently become the new origin just because its title matches.

Source: `packages/database/supabase/schemas/concept.sql:98`, `apps/roam/src/utils/syncDgNodesToSupabase.ts:293`, `apps/roam/src/utils/syncDgNodesToSupabase.ts:1563`.

## UPD-11

Review: **revise steps**

Five failures stop the scheduler; backoff is exponential with jitter. Repeated full reloads reset module state and do not demonstrate the cutoff. Exercise five consecutive failures in one loaded client or use a controlled scheduler test; distinguish error feedback from feedback that scheduling stopped.

Source: `apps/roam/src/utils/syncDgNodesToSupabase.ts:894`, `apps/roam/src/utils/syncDgNodesToSupabase.ts:1664`.

## DEL-04

Review: **supported path**

Read/parse failure becomes an empty relation set; successful full sync reaches orphan deletion. Corrupt/read-failure and intentional empty store must be separate fixtures. Deletion affects all fetched relation IDs, subject to API row limits, so avoid an unconditional all-relations claim for large vaults.

Source: `apps/obsidian/src/utils/relationsStore.ts:35`, `apps/obsidian/src/utils/syncDgNodesToSupabase.ts:480`, `apps/obsidian/src/utils/syncDgNodesToSupabase.ts:736`, `apps/obsidian/src/utils/publishNode.ts:280`.

## REL-10

Review: **supported path**

Ambiguous distinct schema IDs throw and abort the relation stage. Duplicate query patterns for the same schema ID are explicitly deduplicated and are not the same trigger. Seed two real schema IDs plus a valid independent relation.

Source: `apps/roam/src/utils/importSharedRelations.ts:136`, `apps/roam/src/utils/importSharedRelations.ts:243`.

Review: **supported path**

The stored-relation translator matches endpoints/schema without a tentative predicate. Use an accepted relation type with a pending instance so hiding a provisional type does not mask the check.

Source: `apps/roam/src/utils/registerDiscourseDatalogTranslators.ts:498`.

Review: **qualify trigger**

The review list exits when stored relations are disabled; legacy schema enumeration can also omit a relation with no query pattern. Test these settings paths independently and record the graph settings format.

Source: `apps/roam/src/components/TentativeRelationInstances.tsx:54`, `apps/roam/src/utils/getDiscourseRelations.ts:50`.

Review: **supported path**

The Roam relation converter sends local endpoint UIDs even for imported pages. Use disjoint origin/local UIDs and inspect the published relation payload and DB references before checking C. Expand the three platform roles explicitly.

Source: `apps/roam/src/utils/roamToCrossAppConverters.ts:155`, `apps/roam/src/utils/publishNodesToGroups.ts:179`.

Review: **qualify trigger**

Immediate relation publication requires intersecting endpoint publishedToGroups metadata, which imported content may retain. Full-sync grant reconciliation adds another condition. Check right after publish and after the next full sync; separate Roam-origin and Obsidian-origin imports.

Source: `apps/obsidian/src/utils/publishNode.ts:101`, `apps/obsidian/src/utils/publishNode.ts:314`, `apps/obsidian/src/utils/importNodes.ts:1344`.

The suspected visibility mismatch is supported, but the explanation has the identifier direction reversed: local endpoints are stored as constructed RIDs, while getRelationsForFile checks the bare nodeInstanceId and optional importedFromRid. An owned note normally lacks importedFromRid. Assert both panels.

Source: `apps/obsidian/src/utils/relationsStore.ts:246`, `apps/obsidian/src/utils/relationsStore.ts:441`, `apps/obsidian/src/utils/importRelations.ts:263`.

Roam writes nested importedFrom.sourceNodeRid and republishes by filtering importedFromRid. Use local endpoints and an accepted type to avoid the separate provisional-schema exclusion hiding this path.

Source: `apps/roam/src/utils/createReifiedBlock.ts:161`, `apps/roam/src/utils/importSharedRelations.ts:234`, `apps/roam/src/utils/publishNodesToGroups.ts:132`.

Source: `apps/obsidian/src/utils/importPreview.ts:112`, `apps/obsidian/src/utils/importPreview.ts:438`, `apps/obsidian/src/utils/schemaMatching.ts:28`.

Since the formatting is hand-written and irregular, I think the best approach is a Python script that locates each case's block by its id, parses the fields, modifies them, and re-serializes just that block in a consistent layout with id/area/title/dirs, steps, and expected lines.

Now I need to actually apply the review corrections, going case by case. I should check template.html to see how fields render, so I don't add new fields without updating the template. For the J-RR/J-RO/J-OR/J-OO cases I need to add explicit Claim imports before expecting relations, verifying against the referenced code locations, and for SRC-03 I need to update the rating to reflect the settled placeholder evidence.

For PUB-07 I should strip the outdated zero-success claim per the Export.tsx evidence, and for UPD-04 I need to revise the oracle to permit legitimate skipped nodes. SRC-04 needs revised steps, and I have to check whether SRC-06, UPD-10, and UPD-11 are really about avoiding reloads during failure-cutoff tests or actually concern the per-space title uniqueness constraint mentioned in the review. REL-15 needs its identifier explanation corrected, UX-03 and UX-07 need sufficient triggers, DSC-10 and UX-06 need to separate error details from aggregates, and TXT-08 needs a recheck of whether the heading-removal premise is actually obsolete — the rule being not to treat an old implementation detail as if it were unchangeable fact.

For coverage, I'm weighing whether to add a new case for source-space identity collisions in Obsidian discovery, and whether to expand the generic three-space rows into concrete platform assignments, which would require new directory codes like "RRR" and updates to the DIR_TEXT mapping in build.mjs — the review does flag this as unexpanded, so it counts as evidence-backed.

I'm working out the actual dir combinations for each 3S case based on their B assignments (REL-13 with B=R giving RRR/RRO/ORR/ORO, REL-14 with B=O giving ROR/ROO/OOR/OOO), and noting REL-15 and RND-02 overlap, so I need to examine each 3S case individually before deciding whether to extend COL-01/02 with a stable authorship assertion.

Ratings should stay separate from result status, which is already handled correctly, though I might add a clarifying note. For SCL-03/04 pagination tests, I need to revise the steps to reference the app/API boundary properly, and then work through the 43 flagged high-risk entries, folding each review's specific advice — things like using different schema IDs to avoid masking an inconsistency — into the corresponding test steps wherever the review calls for revision or qualification.

I'll incorporate step refinements wherever the review indicates the current steps are insufficient or could mask an issue, including minor fixture advice on otherwise-supported cases since those help prevent false passes; I'll spot-check the key claims against the code at b3796a70 rather than verify everything myself, since bulk evidence-gathering is delegated to Opus subagents while judgment on what to change stays with me.

My plan: pull up all 43 high-risk cases plus the specific ones the review flags, then verify the review's key claims against the candidate worktree code, possibly delegating verification of specific line references to Opus subagents so I can focus on judgment calls. Any case where I disagree with the review, I'll leave as-is and note it in HANDOFF-MATRIX.md for follow-up.

I'm working out the logistics: I need to create the push-pull-repros worktree and get pnpm installed there in parallel with reviewing cases, but entering the worktree changes my cwd, and I recall there's a constraint against cd'ing out of my current directory that I need to respect.

My plan is to kick off worktree creation and the install as a background task first since it's slow, then prepare the six repro case rows while it runs, and once install finishes, launch six subagents to work step 2 while I handle step 1 myself.

Since the review revised the oracle/claim for UPD-04 and REL-15, I should update those rows (along with DEL-04, REL-10, REL-11, REL-13) before handing them to subagents. Let me first check the current git state.

entries.description:
Use this tool ONLY when explicitly instructed to work in a worktree — either by the user directly, or by project instructions (CLAUDE.md / memory). This tool creates an isolated git worktree and switches the current session into it.

## When to Use

- The user explicitly says "worktree" (e.g., "start a worktree", "work in a worktree", "create a worktree", "use a worktree")
- CLAUDE.md or memory instructions direct you to work in a worktree for the current task

## When NOT to Use

- The user asks to create a branch, switch branches, or work on a different branch — use git commands instead
- The user asks to fix a bug or work on a feature — use normal git workflow unless worktrees are explicitly requested by the user or project instructions
- Never use this tool unless "worktree" is explicitly mentioned by the user or in CLAUDE.md / memory instructions

## Requirements

- Must be in a git repository, OR have WorktreeCreate/WorktreeRemove hooks configured in settings.json
- Must not already be in a worktree session when creating a new worktree (`name`); switching into another existing worktree via `path` is allowed

## Behavior

- In a git repository: creates a new git worktree inside `.claude/worktrees/` on a new branch. The base ref is governed by the `worktree.baseRef` setting: `fresh` (default) branches from origin/<default-branch>; `head` branches from your current local HEAD
- Outside a git repository: delegates to WorktreeCreate/WorktreeRemove hooks for VCS-agnostic isolation
- Switches the session's working directory to the new worktree
- Use ExitWorktree to leave the worktree mid-session (keep or remove). On session exit, if still in the worktree, the user will be prompted to keep or remove it

## Entering an existing worktree

Pass `path` instead of `name` to switch the session into a worktree that already exists (e.g., one you just created with `git worktree add`). On first entry from the launch directory, the path must appear in `git worktree list` for the repository that owns it — the current repository or, in a multi-repo workspace, a repository nested inside it; paths registered by neither are rejected. ExitWorktree will not remove a worktree entered this way; use `action: "keep"` to return to the original directory.

Switching with `path` also works when the session is already in a worktree (the previous worktree is left on disk, untouched, and only the new one is tracked for exit-time cleanup), and from agents whose working directory was pinned at launch (subagent isolation or explicit cwd). In both cases the target must be a worktree under `.claude/worktrees/` of the same repository, and from a pinned agent the switch only affects this agent, not the parent session. After a further switch, previously-visited worktrees are no longer writable — re-issue EnterWorktree with `path` to return to one.

## Parameters

- `name` (optional): A name for a new worktree. If neither `name` nor `path` is provided, a random name is generated.
- `path` (optional): Path to an existing worktree to enter instead of creating one — of the current repository, or (on first entry from the launch directory) of a repository nested inside it. Mutually exclusive with `name`.

name.description: Optional name for a new worktree. Each "/"-separated segment may contain only letters, digits, dots, underscores, and dashes; max 64 chars total. A random name is generated if not provided. Mutually exclusive with `path`.

path.description: Path to an existing worktree to switch into instead of creating a new one. Must appear in `git worktree list` for the current repo — or, on first entry from the launch directory, for a repo nested inside it (multi-repo workspace). Mutually exclusive with `name`.

  steps: On an imported page, check the title shows Refresh and no Publish. Then run “DG: Share current node”. Then open a query or canvas “Share Data” dialog whose results include the imported page and use the Publish tab.

recon/database.md:212:- Deleting a Space cascades to all content and access rows; triggers also remove the space's anon auth user, its anon PlatformAccount and its ResourceAccess (`SQL/space.sql:41-56`; `concept.sql:669-680`).

content.thinking:
I realize "access model" was recon describing existing code, not a spec, so the review's point on SEC-04 stands — I should mark it "Not specified" rather than expecting no readable access, and flag it in decisions.md with P1. There's also a real inconsistency worth noting: views require both SpaceAccess and ResourceAccess so they'd hide content after SpaceAccess removal, but tables would still allow access, which is a discrepancy between the two.

My recommendation is that removing a group's SpaceAccess should revoke all reads consistently, tables and storage included, matching what views already do, with explicit ResourceAccess deletion as the separate control. SEC-01/02/05/06 citing "Access model" as src seems fine since those cover obvious security invariants.

While waiting on the agents, I'm now sketching a Python script to edit cases.json — loading it, replacing modified case blocks with re-serialized versions, inserting new cases after a given ID, and formatting the output to match the existing style. Writing case JSON format...

I want to use json.JSONDecoder.raw_decode to locate each object's exact end so I can replace only that block while preserving blank lines and structure elsewhere in the file. I'll hold off writing this until the verification agent responds, and in the meantime I'm drafting decisions.md, compiling the list of P0/P1 decide cases still open after the review — SRC-03 now resolved, plus PUB-04, DEL-03, PUB-11, DSC-06, TXT-04, TXT-06, TTL-11, TTL-15, AST-06, AST-08, UPD-09, REL-05, REL-07, REL-08, REL-09, SEC-03, and the newly added SEC-04.

"""Edit cases.json in place, re-serializing only the cases that change.

Unchanged cases keep their exact bytes. Changed and new cases use the file's
six-line layout. Run with the edits module path as argv[1].
"""

import hashlib
import importlib.util
import json
import sys

PATH = "/mnt/data/projects/dg-validation-eng-1883/matrix/cases.json"
ORDER = ["id", "area", "smoke", "title", "dirs", "steps", "expected", "src",
         "rating", "why", "ev", "method", "evidence", "pri", "iso"]


def j(v):
    return json.dumps(v, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"))


def serialize(c):
    unknown = set(c) - set(ORDER)
    assert not unknown, unknown
    head = [f'"id":{j(c["id"])}', f'"area":{j(c["area"])}']
    if c.get("smoke"):
        head.append('"smoke":true')
    head += [f'"title":{j(c["title"])}', f'"dirs":{j(c["dirs"])}']
    tail = [f'"ev":{j(c["ev"])}', f'"method":{j(c["method"])}',
            f'"evidence":{j(c["evidence"])}', f'"pri":{j(c["pri"])}']
    if c.get("iso"):
        tail.append('"iso":true')
    return (
        "{" + ",".join(head) + ",\n"
        f' "steps":{j(c["steps"])},\n'
        f' "expected":{j(c["expected"])},\n'
        f' "src":{j(c["src"])},"rating":{j(c["rating"])},\n'
        f' "why":{j(c["why"])},\n'
        " " + ",".join(tail) + "}"
    )


def spans(text):
    dec = json.JSONDecoder()
    out = {}
    i = text.index("[") + 1
    while True:
        k = text.find('{"id":', i)
        if k < 0:
            break
        obj, end = dec.raw_decode(text, k)
        out[obj["id"]] = (k, end, obj)
        i = end
    return out


def main():
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("edits", sys.argv[1])
    edits = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(edits)

    text = open(PATH, encoding="utf8").read()
    before = hashlib.sha256(text.encode()).hexdigest()
    sp = spans(text)

    # Changes: id -> dict of field updates (None deletes the field).
    repl = []
    for cid, upd in edits.CHANGES.items():
        k, end, obj = sp[cid]
        new = dict(obj)
        for f, v in upd.items():
            if v is None:
                new.pop(f, None)
            else:
                new[f] = v
        assert new["id"] == cid
        repl.append((k, end, serialize(new)))

    # Additions: list of (after_id, case)
    for after, case in edits.ADDITIONS:
        assert case["id"] not in sp, case["id"]
        k, end, _ = sp[after]
        repl.append((end, end, ",\n" + serialize(case)))

    repl.sort(key=lambda r: (r[0], r[1]))
    out, pos = [], 0
    for k, end, s in repl:
        assert k >= pos, "overlapping edits"
        out.append(text[pos:k])
        out.append(s)
        pos = end
    out.append(text[pos:])
    result = "".join(out)

    data = json.loads(result)
    ids = [c["id"] for c in data]
    assert len(ids) == len(set(ids)), "duplicate ids"
    orig_ids = [c["id"] for c in json.loads(text)]
    assert all(i in ids for i in orig_ids), "lost an id"
    for c in data:
        for f in ["id", "area", "title", "dirs", "steps", "expected", "src",
                  "rating", "why", "ev", "method", "evidence", "pri"]:
            assert f in c, (c["id"], f)
        assert c["rating"] in {"risk", "decide", "gap", "pass", "unknown"}, c["id"]
        assert c["method"] in {"bash", "db", "auto"}, c["id"]
        assert c["evidence"] in {"shot", "log", "receipt"}, c["id"]
        assert c["pri"] in {"P0", "P1", "P2"}, c["id"]
    open(PATH, "w", encoding="utf8").write(result)
    after = hashlib.sha256(result.encode()).hexdigest()
    print(f"before={before}\nafter={after}\ncases={len(data)} changed={len(edits.CHANGES)} added={len(edits.ADDITIONS)}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

  **REL-13: reproduced on the producer side.** On candidate `b3796a70`, all 12 tests fail. Each failure shows Roam sending B's local page uid where A1's origin record should be.
  
  **Expected (from the row):** B's published relation points at A1's origin record, meaning a RID that resolves to A's space and A1's origin id. C then sees the A1–B1 relation as pending.
  
  **Actual:** In every case (A is Roam or Obsidian, relation in either direction), the imported endpoint is sent as `bCopyOfA1Uid`, B's local page uid.
  - **Conversion:** `reifiedRelationToCrossApp` (`roamToCrossAppConverters.ts:167-175`) copies `sourceUid`/`destinationUid` as they are.
  - **Publish:** publishing B1 selects the relation and sends `local_reference_content={"source":"B1pageUid","destination":"bCopyOfA1Uid"}` (or the reverse) through `crossAppRelationToDbConcept` (`crossAppConverters.ts:193-196`).
  - **Selection throws away the RID:** the publish code reads A1's origin RID from `importedFrom` only to check that A1 came from a space the group knows (`publishNodesToGroups.ts:109-115`, `:184`, `:187`).
  - **The fix already exists nearby:** the contract allows a RID endpoint (`crossAppContracts.ts:119-120`), and the source-slot path already swaps an imported page for its RID (`sourceSlot.ts:107-110`).
  - **The candidate's one-line change** in `crossAppConverters.ts` (line 101, the node-schema `label`) has nothing to do with relation endpoints.
  
  **What the database would do (read from `concept.sql`, not run):** it rejects the relation rather than leaving it dangling.
  - A bare id is looked up only in B's space (`concept.sql:325-328`, `:352-353`). B's space has no record for the imported copy, because sync skips imported pages (`syncDgNodesToSupabase.ts:1432-1440`).
  - The failed lookup makes `reference_content` NULL (`:441-447`, because `jsonb_set` returns NULL on a NULL value). That breaks the NOT NULL column (`:62`), and `upsert_concepts` returns -2 (`:586-589`).
  - With -2, publish withholds the relation's access grant (`publishNodesToGroups.ts:394-411`, `:441-447`). The third group of tests models that -2 and confirms the grant for the relation is withheld. Without a grant, C can't see the relation. I did not trace C's import side.
  
  **Surprises:**
  - `publishNodesToGroups.ts:479` still reports a relation as published even when its upsert failed. Nothing in `apps/roam/src` reads that field.
  - The real `orderConceptsByDependency` flags `bCopyOfA1Uid` as a missing dependency, but publish ignores that list (`:363`).
  
  **Coverage:** the producer half of all four assignments (RRR, RRO, ORR, ORO). B is Roam in all of them, and both A RID shapes are tested: Roam URL and `orn:obsidian.note:`. C's platform is not exercised.

Discourse Graphs · Roam and Obsidian push and pull · Internal validation

Push/pull test matrix

Every case for sharing nodes between Roam graphs and Obsidian vaults, with each app as source and destination. Ratings come from reading the code at the candidate commit. They say where to look first; they don't decide the result.

Candidate
push-pull-validation-head at b3796a70
Base
main 4a13294a
Merged in
#1383 ENG-2131, #1475 ENG-2202, #1477 ENG-2288, #1479 ENG-2296, #1482 Obsidian file names
Checks
pnpm ci:validate passed
Code read
2026-09-25

Run these first

High-risk cases at P0 and P1. Code reading suggests the expected result won't hold. Cases marked “isolated” need a throwaway space.

    Decide before testing

    The tickets don't settle what should happen. Get a decision, then test against it. These are product questions, not bugs.

      Before you start
      • Same candidate for everyone. Build the Roam extension and the Obsidian plugin from b3796a70. Results only count for the commit they tested.
      • Spaces. At least two Roam graphs and two Obsidian vaults, one more space for the three-space cases, and one space outside the test group for access checks. Use two groups: G1 for everyone and G2 for a subset.
      • Accounts. Everyone in a Roam graph uses that graph's database account, and each vault has its own. Group membership belongs to a graph or vault, not to a person.
      • Roam settings. Turn on Node sharing and the Suggestive mode overlay (import needs it until ENG-2297), and keep stored relations on (the pending-relations list needs them). Reload after any change. Suggestive mode also changes what syncs, so note which mode each result used.
      • Obsidian settings. In the plugin settings press Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+A to open the Admin panel, turn on “(BETA) Sync mode enable”, then reload. For Source cases, the vault needs a node type named “Source” and an accepted relation type from Evidence to Source.
      • Timing. Roam syncs about every 5 minutes, at least 130 s apart across clients; reloading the graph syncs right away. Obsidian syncs 5 s after the last edit, and fully on load and on publish. Destinations only change when you press Refresh.
      • Isolated cases break or delete data on purpose. Run them on throwaway spaces and a throwaway group, never on a graph people use.
      • Access-control cases (SEC) run only against a local database, by an engineer. File confirmed ones as private Linear tickets, not public GitHub issues.
      Recording results
      • Where things live. ENG-1881 holds the cases, fixtures and expected behavior. ENG-1883 holds one record per candidate run with results, blockers and links. Each failure gets a bug ticket with a minimal repro and its video. Fix PRs carry the regression check and the passing repro.
      • A pass needs a receipt: case, direction, candidate commit, environment, tester and what you saw. “Refresh updated the existing page uid and kept one Source relation” beats “passed”. Add a screenshot when the result is visual.
      • On a failure, capture it right away: steps, actual result, the spaces and accounts involved, console logs and fixture state. Record the video later, in the recording session, from a check that states the expected result, so the fix PR can rerun the same check.
      • Merge videos only once you know two failures share a cause. Similar failures in Roam and Obsidian can have different causes.
      • New candidate: rerun the affected cases plus the four journeys. Earlier evidence stays valid for the commit it tested; a rebase alone doesn't need new videos.
      Fixtures

      Roam

      • Source “@Fixture Source 2026”, Claim “[[CLM]] - Fixture claim”, and Evidence “[[EVD]] - Fixture rich text - [[@Fixture Source 2026]]” with a stored relation to the Claim.
      • Evidence body: **bold**, __italic__, ^^highlight^^, ~~strike~~, inline code; an external link, [[Some page]], #tag, #[[multi word tag]]; a block ref and an embed; {{[[TODO]]}} and {{[[DONE]]}}; four levels of nested bullets; a numbered list; heading blocks; a code block with a language; $$E=mc^2$$; a quote; Key:: value; {{[[table]]}}; an uploaded image, {{[[pdf]]: …}}, {{[[video]]: …}}, {{[[audio]]: …}}; café, 日本語, 🧪.

      Obsidian

      • A Source note, an Evidence note with a relation to it, and a Claim with a relation from the Evidence.
      • Evidence note: frontmatter with nodeTypeId and one custom key; # and ## headings; **bold**, *italic*, ==highlight==, ~~strike~~; [[Note]], [[Note|alias]], [[Note#Heading]], [[Note#^block]], #tag, #nested/tag; tasks; nested bullets; a numbered list; a > [!note] callout; a table; a footnote; %% comment %%; $$math$$; a fenced code block; ![[image.png]], ![[doc.pdf]], ![[doc.pdf#page=2]], ![[clip.mp4]], ![[voice.mp3]], [[report.docx]]; a note embed; a horizontal rule.

      Assets

      • png, jpg, gif and svg images; PDFs of 1 MiB, exactly 6 MiB (6,291,456 bytes) and 7 MiB; a short mp4 and mp3; docx, csv and zip files; one image used in two nodes; two different files both named image.png.
      Direction
      Rating
      Method
      Priority
      Show

      Six code readers went through the candidate commit, the Linear tickets and the PR threads. The four most serious claims were re-checked by hand: refresh-all counting relation blocks, the empty relations file deleting relations, the account-in-space function granting editor, and the group membership insert rule.

entries.description: Retrieve detailed information about an issue by ID, including attachments, git branch name, and active Triage Intelligence suggestions when the issue is in triage

id.description: Issue ID or identifier (e.g., LIN-123). P-prefixed identifiers (e.g., P-ENG-123) are projects, not issues

entries.name: mcp__linear-server__list_comments
entries.description: List comments on a Linear issue, project, initiative, document, project milestone, or project/initiative status update. Provide exactly one of `issueId`, `projectId`, `initiativeId`, `documentId`, `milestoneId`, or `statusUpdateId`. For issues, projects, and initiatives this returns both top-level discussion threads and inline description comments. Inline (anchored) comments carry a non-null `quotedText` set to the snippet of description text they reference. Returned comments include `author` and nullable `onBehalfOf`; when set, `onBehalfOf` identifies the user the agent author acted for. Files uploaded in comment bodies are returned in `attachments` with titles and download URLs, not issue attachment IDs. Signed upload URLs expire after five minutes; call list_comments again to refresh them. Download documents using these URLs and process them with your own file tools.

issueId.description: Issue ID or identifier (e.g., LIN-123). P-prefixed identifiers (e.g., P-ENG-123) are projects, not issues (provide exactly one parent)

projectId.description: Project name, ID, identifier (e.g., P-ENG-123), or slug (provide exactly one parent)

initiativeId.description: Initiative name, ID, identifier (e.g., I-123), or slug (provide exactly one parent)

documentId.description: Document ID or slug (provide exactly one parent)

milestoneId.description: Milestone UUID (provide exactly one parent). Resolve milestone names via `list_milestones` first.

statusUpdateId.description: Status update UUID (provide exactly one parent). Resolve status updates via `get_status_updates` first.

statusUpdateType.description: Type of status update named by `statusUpdateId`, as returned by `get_status_updates`. Only valid together with `statusUpdateId`; omit to check both project and initiative status updates.

# DG Engineering Writing Style

Write in a direct, concise, plainspoken style that preserves important context and qualification.

## Core style

- Lead with the relevant point and move quickly to the concrete question, request, or action.
- Prefer the shortest version that remains clear and preserves necessary nuance.
- Identify wording or missing context that is ambiguous or could be misconstrued. Resolve it when the intended meaning is clear; otherwise, flag it and ask for clarification.
- Use natural contractions and everyday wording. Avoid corporate jargon, inflated phrasing, and generic professional filler.
- Avoid em dashes as sentence-level punctuation. Use a period, comma, colon, semicolon, or parentheses to separate thoughts instead. Preserve em dashes only when they appear in exact quotations, titles, source text, or technical content supplied by the requester.

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

When an event lands that the user would want to act on now — an error appeared, the status they were waiting on flipped — send a PushNotification. Not every event is worth a push; the ones that change what they'd do next are.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

content.content:
## Expected (case row)

No failures from the relation block or type pages. Totals count only imported nodes. Unchanged nodes are skipped, the edited node is refreshed, and nothing fails.

## Actual on the candidate

Setup, all through real code: two related source nodes are imported (`getSharedNodeByRid` + `materializeSharedNode`), then `importSharedRelations` runs. The import leaves five entities carrying the import marker: two node pages, one node-type page (`discourse-graph/nodes/Claim`), one relation-type block, and one relation block.

| Run | `refreshAllImportedNodes()` returns (OR and RR identical) | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| 1, sources unchanged | `{"refreshed":0,"skipped":2,"failed":3,"warnings":[]}` | `{refreshed:0, skipped:2, failed:0, warnings:[]}` |
| 2, node B edited at source | `{"refreshed":1,"skipped":1,"failed":3,"warnings":[]}` | `{refreshed:1, skipped:1, failed:0, warnings:[]}` |

What each entry's refresh did (same in both runs and both directions):

| Entry | Status | Message (dropped by Refresh all) | Writes to it |
|---|---|---|---|
| node page A | skipped | `"CLM - Sleep consolidates memory" is already up to date.` | none |
| node page B | run 1 skipped, run 2 refreshed | run 2: `Refreshed "CLM - REM sleep predicts recall" from <space>.` | run 2: `block.fromMarkdown`, `block.update` (new content, new source time) |
| node-type page | failed | `The source of "discourse-graph/nodes/Claim" is no longer shared with your groups, so it cannot be refreshed.` | none, props unchanged |
| relation-type block | failed | `The source of "" is no longer shared with your groups, so it cannot be refreshed.` | none, props unchanged |
| relation block | failed | `The source of "" is no longer shared with your groups, so it cannot be refreshed.` | none, props unchanged |

Test results: 4 failed, 6 passed out of 10.

- Failed, as expected where the issue reproduces: both "expected (case row)" tests in each direction. Each fails on `failed: 3` and on the list of three non-node failures. The node-level assertions in the same tests pass: A skipped, B skipped then refreshed, and B's page holds the edited body.
- Passed: the "why" checks below.

## Result: reproduced

The node part of the expected result holds. Unchanged nodes are skipped, and the edited node is refreshed with its new content. The totals are wrong: every imported relation block, relation-type block and node-type page is counted, and each counts as `failed`. With two nodes and one relation, the toast would read `0 refreshed, 2 skipped, 3 failed.` with warning intent and no reason given.

## What the code confirms or contradicts in the row's "why"

Confirmed:
- Refresh all enumerates every entity that carries the marker, pages and blocks alike. The query in `apps/roam/src/utils/importedSourceIdentity.ts:82-88` binds `?page` only through `:block/uid` and `:block/props` plus the `discourse-graph → importedFrom → sourceNodeRid` chain. It has no `:node/title`, `:block/page` or `:block/parents` clause, and the test asserts the exact clause list. `refreshAllImportedNodes.ts:13,20-22` refreshes each uid and adds one to the matching count.
- The marker writers put the same `importedFrom {sourceModifiedAt, sourceNodeRid}` prop on non-node entities: the node-type page at `importSharedRelations.ts:62-71`, the relation-type block at `:150-162`, and the relation block at `:228-238`, which carries it next to `sourceUid/destinationUid/hasSchema`. The test runs the real `importSharedRelations` and reads the marker back with the real `readImportedSourceIdentity`.
- Each non-node entry counts as failed. `refreshImportedNode.ts:28-33` finds a valid identity, so the entry isn't rejected as "no identity". Then `getSharedNodeByRid` (`packages/database/src/lib/sharedNodes.ts:357-364`) queries concepts with `is_schema = false` and `is_relation = false`. That excludes relation instances (`is_relation` true, see `discoverSharedRelations.ts:47-48` and `packages/database/supabase/schemas/concept.sql:35-45`), relation schemas (`discoverSharedRelations.ts:148-149`) and node schemas. The function returns `null`, and `refreshImportedNode.ts:46-50` returns `failed`. In the fake DB, the relation and schema entities also have content rows, so the failure comes from the concept filters alone.
- "No reason shown" is confirmed. `refreshAllImportedNodes.ts:23-24` passes on only `result.warning`, never a failure `message`, and the toast (`registerCommandPaletteCommands.ts:390-397`) shows only the counts plus warnings. That path doesn't call `internalError` either (`refreshImportedNode.ts:46-50`).
- Skipped is not a failure: the unchanged node goes through `materializeSharedNode.ts:431-445` and returns `skipped`.

Corrected or refined:
- The reason, if anyone saw it, would be wrong. It says the source "is no longer shared with your groups", but the source is still shared. It just isn't a node. For blocks the title is empty (`The source of ""`), because `refreshImportedNode.ts:27` reads `:node/title`, which blocks don't have.
- Refresh writes nothing to the relation block, relation-type block or node-type page. The failure returns before `materializeSharedNode`, and the test records no Roam write and no props change on those uids.
- The row says "relation-type and node-type pages", but the imported relation type is a block under the grammar's `relations` node (`createRelationSchema.ts:24-44`), not a page. Only the node type is a page (`accessors.ts:1144-1147`). Both carry the marker and both fail.
- The failed count grows with every imported relation, relation type and node type, not just by a fixed amount per import.

## Limits

- There is no Datalog engine. The fake `data.async.q` evaluates the marker chain the query reads over every in-memory entity. It would restrict to titled pages only if the query had a `:node/title` clause. The claim that real Roam returns blocks for this query rests on reading the query text, not on running it in Roam.
