content.content: Launching skill: artifact-design

content.text:
## Page contract — read before your first publish

These are the Artifact tool's own rules for the file you publish; the design guidance below builds on them.

**Format**: Always author the page as `.html`. Publish a `.md` file only when a loaded skill explicitly instructs it. When the user shares a markdown document or asks to turn one into an artifact, author an HTML page based on its content — preserve its substance, and design the page as you would any other artifact rather than transcribing the markdown one-to-one.

**Skeleton**: The file is wrapped in a `<!doctype html>…<head>…</head><body>` skeleton at publish time, so write the page content directly — no `<!DOCTYPE>`, `<html>`, `<head>`, or `<body>` tags of your own. Its head carries only a charset and viewport meta (with `viewport-fit=cover`) plus a small reset — light `color-scheme`, `:root` padded top and bottom by the phone's safe-area insets, zero body margin with a 14px system font on an off-white ground, `img{max-width:100%}`, and `[hidden]{display:none!important}` (toggle visibility with `el.hidden`, not `style.display`) — so put your own `<title>` and `<style>` at the top of the file. Keep the `:root` padding: a bar fixed to the top or bottom stays at `0` and adds `env(safe-area-inset-top, 0px)` or `env(safe-area-inset-bottom, 0px)` to its own padding, and a sticky page header uses `top: env(safe-area-inset-top, 0px)`, not `0`.

**Title**: Set a `<title>` at the top of the HTML — only the first 8KB of the file is scanned for it. It names the artifact in the browser tab and gallery, so make it a name, not a summary: a short noun phrase, typically two to four words, distinctive to this page's subject so the reader can pick it out of a gallery of many — the way an app or a document gets named, never a generic category label, and never a name plus an appended explainer after a dash or colon. When a natural title pairs the name with a generic word, the name is the half that survives the trim — keeping the generic half and dropping the identity makes the title worse, not shorter. And trim only actual explainers: a multi-word title that already reads as one specific name is finished as it is. The explanation belongs in the `description` parameter instead: pass a one-sentence `description` — it becomes the gallery card's subtitle. For HTML publishes, a `title` parameter fills in when the file has no tag (Markdown pages always keep their filename identity). Keep the title stable across redeploys.

**External resources — CDN allowlist (CSP-enforced)**: external scripts load ONLY from https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com (preferred), https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/, https://unpkg.com, https://cdn.tailwindcss.com (Tailwind's play-CDN script) and https://code.jquery.com; external stylesheets ONLY from https://fonts.googleapis.com, with the font files they pull from https://fonts.gstatic.com (give every face a real fallback stack). Everything else is blocked, with no visible error: every other host (esm.sh included) and, even on those CDNs, anything but a script — stylesheets, images, media, fetch/XHR/WebSocket, a library's runtime fetches. So inline all other CSS and JS and embed assets as data: URIs. **How to load a library**: `<script src="https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/<lib>/<exact version>/<file>">` — pick the UMD build, which defines a global (e.g. react/18.3.1/umd/react.production.min.js, then react-dom) — placed BEFORE any inline `<script>` that uses it; always pin an exact version. The viewer's sandbox also blocks any download the page starts itself — `<a download>` links (data:/blob: hrefs included) and script-driven saves are inert for viewers — so never offer a file through a plain link. Links to other websites (`https://…`) open in a new tab, but email, phone and app links (`mailto:`, `tel:`, `sms:`, other custom schemes) are unreliable inside an artifact: for many viewers (for example anyone outside the user's organization, or anyone viewing through a public link) following one, by link or by script, often does not work, and the page cannot tell whether it did. So show the address or number itself as selectable text (a copy button helps), treat such a link as a convenience that may do nothing, and never tell the viewer a message was sent or a call placed because the viewer tapped one. Artifacts render mermaid diagrams natively — markdown via ```mermaid fences, HTML via `<pre class="mermaid">` blocks — no library needed, don't load one. The viewer never shows `alert()`, `confirm()` or `prompt()` dialogs — `confirm()` returns false and `prompt()` returns null immediately — so build any confirmation step into the page itself.

**What the viewer's frame allows**: The page runs in a locked-down frame; what it refuses below, it refuses for every viewer (anonymous, signed-in, embedded, desktop and mobile apps), so build around these limits instead of detecting them. The page cannot open the print dialog — `window.print()` does nothing — so never offer a Print or "Save as PDF" button. Forms work as page UI (inputs, validation, submit events), but a real submission has nowhere to go: handle `submit` in script with `preventDefault()` and never point `action` at another site or a mailto: address. Copy buttons work when `navigator.clipboard.writeText` is called inside the click handler — catch its rejection (older desktop apps and some app views refuse it) and fall back to selecting the text; reading the clipboard never works, though the viewer's own Paste (the `paste` event) does. Camera, microphone, screen capture, location, Web Share and similar device APIs are refused without a prompt — don't build features on them (a screen wake lock may be granted while the page is visible: request it and tolerate rejection); file inputs, drag-and-drop of files and `FileReader` work in browsers, so take photos, audio and data as uploaded files instead. Fullscreen and pointer lock work from a click in desktop browsers; treat both as optional (handle the rejection) since phones and some app views lack them. Sound plays only after the viewer interacts (muted autoplay is fine), so start audio from a button. Other sites cannot be embedded — no YouTube, map or form iframes, and no `<object>`/`<embed>`; link out instead: links open outside the artifact, normally in a new tab, while `window.open` works only for some signed-in viewers in the artifact's own organization and returns null for everyone else, so use real `<a href>` links. Web Workers work from your own files or `blob:` URLs; service workers and WebRTC do not. `fetch()` of files published alongside the page works with relative URLs; images from your own files, `data:` or `blob:` URLs draw to canvas and export cleanly. Only a plain `#anchor` (letters, digits, `.` `_` `~` `-`) from the artifact's link reaches `location.hash` — never `#key=value` state and never the query string — so deep-link to a tab or section with a bare token and keep all other state in the page.

**Browser storage**: `localStorage` (also `sessionStorage` and IndexedDB) works, but each artifact has its own origin and the data lives only in that viewer's browser — it survives republishes to the same URL and never reaches other viewers, other devices, or Claude. It can come back empty or the accessor can throw (a private window, cleared or blocked site data, previews or thumbnail capture), so wrap every read and write in try/catch and render the page correctly without it. Use it only for per-viewer conveniences (a remembered tab or filter, a collapsed section, an unsent draft), never for state that must persist reliably, be shared between viewers, or be read back by Claude — state like that belongs in a runtime capability when this user has one: load the `artifact-capabilities` skill before writing the page.

**Size**: The rendered page must be 16MB or smaller, and embedded data: URIs count toward that.

**Responsive**: The page must also work at phone width (~400px). Keep a side gutter of at least 16px at every width: set it once as side padding on `body` or one outer wrapper, and give that element any vertical padding with `padding-block`, never a `padding` shorthand that zeroes the sides. Use relative units; let flex/grid rows wrap or stack to one column when narrow; put `max-width:100%` on images and on any `aspect-ratio` box, and no `min-width` wider than the screen on anything. Only tables, diagrams and code blocks may be wider, each inside its own `overflow-x: auto` container — the page body must never scroll horizontally.

**Theme-aware**: Pages render in the viewer's theme, which has three states: an explicit choice stamps `data-theme="dark"` / `data-theme="light"` on the root element, and the default "system" setting stamps nothing — only `prefers-color-scheme` separates light from dark. Define the complete light palette as tokens on bare `:root` (dark-first designs swap the roles consistently); redefine only the tokens under `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)`, guarded as `:root:not([data-theme="light"])`; redefine them again under `:root[data-theme="dark"]` so the toggle wins in both directions, and set `color-scheme: dark` wherever the dark palette applies — both dark blocks, or bare `:root` in a dark-first or single-dark design (the skeleton pins `light` on `:root`) — so form controls and scrollbars follow. Never give a color its only definition inside a media or `[data-theme]` block, and give `body` an explicit token background — the viewer paints its own ground behind the page, so a transparent body borrows the host's theme. A design that deliberately commits to a single look may skip the dark blocks but still paints background and colors explicitly.

**Icon** (on every first publish): Pass one short generic word as `icon` (e.g. `"chart"`, `"calendar"`, `"recipe"`) for the artifact's browser-tab icon — a plain signifier for what the page is, never a product or brand name, and never an emoji or markup. It stays the **same** for the life of an artifact, so on a redeploy (the same file path this session, or `url`) omit `icon` and the artifact keeps the one it has; pass a different one only when the user asks.

Work the way the design lead at a small, versatile studio would: give each client a visual identity at the level of treatment the task calls for. Make deliberate choices about palette, typography, and layout that are specific to this subject, and avoid templated designs.

## Read the request first

Decide the treatment; designing is a given. A doc gets the same craft as a landing page; only the treatment differs. Format is a separate matter: author HTML, and publish Markdown only when a loaded skill explicitly instructs it. A Markdown publish keeps its filename as its title, uses almost none of the craft below, and is never a way to save time.

Many requests call for a more utilitarian treatment: a plan, a memo, a demo. Make it polished, with real typographic hierarchy, considered spacing, and a proper palette, but avoid over-designing. Most pages don't need a flashy, gigantic hero. Keep flourishes tasteful and limited.

Some requests call for an editorial treatment: a landing page, a game, an app or tool they'll keep or share.

If unsure: a well-composed page is always acceptable; an over-designed visual identity sometimes isn't.

Fundamentals below apply to everything. Follow the editorial process after them only when that reading calls for it.

## Fundamentals for every artifact

**Respect what already exists.** Look for an existing design system first: CLAUDE.md, a tokens or theme file, existing component styles. When one exists, apply it; everything below fills gaps and never overrides. Precedence is always the user's own words, then the project's existing system, then your choices.

**Ground it in the subject.** If the subject isn't already clear, define it: one concrete subject, its audience, and the page's single job. Distinctive choices come from the subject's own world: its materials, instruments, and vernacular. Whatever the treatment, include at least one detail only this subject would have (its real units and scales, its document conventions, its terms of art) as content rather than ornament; it costs nothing even on a plain page. Use real content throughout and never lorem ipsum.

**Pair typefaces.** Typography determines how the page reads even when the page isn't about typography. Google Fonts is the only font host the Artifact CSP allows; link it directly (`<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=...&display=swap">`). A face from anywhere else must be inlined as a @font-face data URI, or the browser silently uses a fallback. In both cases, declare a real fallback stack. Keep running text near 65 characters wide. Set a type scale and keep to it. Give headings `text-wrap: balance`, give body text comfortable spacing, and give uppercase labels a little letter-spacing.

**Load libraries instead of inlining them.** When the page really needs a library (React, a charting or highlighting package), load its UMD build from cdnjs with one pinned `<script src="https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/...">` placed before the inline script that uses its global; don't inline the library's source or hand-write a substitute. Only the script loads this way; a library's stylesheet still has to be inlined, and the page contract above lists the few other script hosts the CSP admits. The page's own CSS and JS, its images, and its data ship with the page. Most pages don't need any library; use one only when it does substantial work for the page.

**Choose neutrals deliberately.** A pure mid-grey looks unconsidered; a grey with a slight hue bias toward the page's accent looks intentional. Pure white and near-black are fine backgrounds when they suit the subject, as long as you chose the neutral deliberately instead of inheriting a default.

**Design both themes.** The page renders in the viewer's theme, and the viewer has three states: an explicit choice sets `data-theme="dark"` or `data-theme="light"` on the root element, and the default "system" setting sets *nothing*. Most viewers see the document with no `data-theme` attribute, where only `prefers-color-scheme` distinguishes light from dark. Structure the CSS at the token level for all three. The bare `:root` block defines the complete light palette (for a deliberately dark-first design, swap light and dark consistently through this whole pattern); `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` redefines only the tokens, guarded as `:root:not([data-theme="light"])` so an explicit light choice overrides a dark OS setting; `:root[data-theme="dark"]` redefines them again so the toggle also overrides in the other direction; wherever the dark palette applies - both dark blocks, or bare `:root` in a dark-first or single-dark design - also set `color-scheme: dark` (the skeleton pins `light` on `:root`), so native form controls and scrollbars follow the palette. Style components through the tokens, never directly inside a media or `[data-theme]` block: a color defined only inside `[data-theme]` never applies when no `data-theme` attribute is set, and the page then shows one theme's text on the other theme's background. Two more rules keep each theme consistent. First, the artifact is composited over a background the viewer paints in *its own* theme, so `body` must set an explicit `background` from a token; a transparent body shows the host's background with no warning. Second, every element that sets a color takes it from the same token set as the surface behind it, never from a literal that works in only one theme. Declare every token in the bare `:root` block before any media or `[data-theme]` block redefines it; a color that exists only inside one of those blocks is the classic unreadable-artifact bug. Give the second theme the same care as the first: don't simply invert it; keep contrast legible and keep the accent working on both backgrounds. A design that deliberately commits to one visual world (a neon arcade screen, a letterpress invitation) may stay single-theme: then omit the media query and `[data-theme]` blocks entirely but still set the background and every color explicitly, so the page looks right on either host background; do this by choice, never by omission.

**Use layout for spacing.** Lay out sibling groups with flex or grid and `gap` instead of per-element margins, which collapse or double without warning. Keep a side gutter of at least 16px at every width: set it once as side padding on `body` or one outer wrapper, whose vertical padding uses `padding-block` and never a `padding` shorthand that zeroes the sides. Let rows wrap or stack to one column at phone width (about 400px). Give images and any `aspect-ratio` box `max-width: 100%`, and don't give anything a `min-width` wider than the screen. Only wide tables, code, and diagrams may exceed it; give each `overflow-x: auto` on its own container so the page body never scrolls sideways. The publish skeleton pads `:root` top and bottom by the phone's safe-area insets (zero everywhere except a phone app) so the page runs edge to edge while its content stays clear of the system bars; keep that padding. A bar fixed to the top or bottom stays at `0` and adds `env(safe-area-inset-top, 0px)` or `env(safe-area-inset-bottom, 0px)` to its own padding. A sticky page header uses `top: env(safe-area-inset-top, 0px)` and never `0`. Size a one-screen app with `height: 100%` on `html` and `body` instead of `100vh`, so it fits inside that padding. A page that includes its own viewport meta gets this padding only when that meta declares `viewport-fit=cover`. Use `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` wherever digits line up in columns.

**Make repeated elements consistent.** For cards in a row, label/value pairs down a list, or badges on sibling items, use the same edges, baselines, and inner padding on each, and put any recurring element in the same place on each. Let content set a container's height and pick a column count the items fill, so nothing stretches over empty space or sits alone in a row. Make text that can outgrow its track wrap or scroll in its own container; clipped text is a bug.

**Use card styling selectively.** Border, fill, radius, and shadow each mark an element as a separate object. Apply them by role, to set off the one element that needs it; applying the same radius and shadow to every block flattens the hierarchy. Open with big-number tiles only when those figures are the point of the page.

**Draw charts to scale.** Place marks, ticks, and labels with one scale, and make every label name a value the chart actually reaches. Color chart text from the theme tokens so it is readable in both themes. Keep marks, labels, and edges clear of one another and inside the drawing's bounds; in SVG, leave room in the viewBox for the outermost labels and give every drawn shape an explicit fill.

**Make the page complete at rest.** Everything meant to be read is visible once the page has loaded, with no scrolling to trigger it; that first still frame is what a thumbnail, a shared link, and a skimming reader all see. A section may animate in, but from a visible resting state, never left at `opacity: 0` waiting for an observer. Size a hero to its content instead of to the viewport; a `100vh` opener pushes the rest of the page out of that first frame. A tool or app opens in a realistic working state: the user's real data where it exists, otherwise example rows, a loaded sample, or a plausibly filled form, clearly marked as examples and never presented as the user's own figures. The first view shows what the tool does; an empty shell waiting for input shows nothing.

**Avoid AI-generated design.** AI-generated design currently clusters around a few looks: warm cream (#F4F1EA) with a serif display and terracotta accent; near-black with a lone acid-green or vermilion pop; broadsheet hairline rules with dense columns; a purple-to-blue gradient hero on white; Inter or Space Grotesk as the "safe" face; emoji as section markers; everything centered; `rounded-lg` everywhere; accent bar/rail on rounded cards. When the user specifies a visual direction, follow it exactly; their words always win, including when they ask for one of these looks. When nothing is specified, don't use that freedom on one of these defaults.

**Build cleanly.** Watch for overlapping elements, cascade collisions, and silent font fallbacks. Close every non-void element, double-quote attributes, give keyboard focus a visible state, and respect `prefers-reduced-motion`. Give every form control a stable `id` (the platform preserves form values, focus, and scroll position across a republish). For generative or decorative graphics, use Canvas or WebGL instead of hand-writing long SVG path data.

**CSS rules.** When writing the CSS, watch your selector specificity. It is easy to generate classes that cancel each other out, e.g. a type-based selector like `.section` and an element-based one like `.cta` both setting padding and margins between sections. Structure the cascade so it doesn't undo your spacing unnoticed.

**Writing the copy.** Treat words as design material and never as decoration. Write from the user's side of the screen: name things by what people recognize instead of how the system is built (a person manages *notifications*; they don't manage *webhook config*). Use active voice; a control states exactly what happens ("Publish", then a toast that says "Published"). Errors explain what went wrong and how to fix it, without apologies or vagueness. Prefer specific to clever. Write plainly, the way a knowledgeable person would talk. Avoid mannered devices: asides set off by em-dashes, "not X, but Y" framing, colon-then-reveal sentences, scare quotes around invented labels, and stock phrases such as "worth noting" or "honest caveat". Prefer short, direct sentences over compressed or clever phrasing.

**Name the page like a product; don't caption it.** The `<title>` is the artifact's name in the gallery and the browser tab, and it gives the reader a first impression of the care taken. Give the page a real name: a short noun phrase, typically two to four words, specific to the subject; or, for a page that exists to answer one question, that question itself, which then is the page's name. Stop at the name; a title that adds its own explanation after a dash or colon reads as generated filler. The name must also identify the page among many: in the gallery it appears beside dozens of other artifacts, and a generic category label that could apply to any of them fails as a name just as an appended explanation does. When a candidate title combines the name with a generic word (a greeting, a category, a page-type label), keep the name; a trim that drops the identifying part and keeps the generic word produces a title that could apply to any page. This rule removes explanations and doesn't require brevity: a multi-word title that already reads as one specific name is finished, and shortening it further only makes it generic. Put the explanation in the one-sentence publish `description`; the gallery shows it directly under the title.

**Structure is information.** Structural devices (numbering, eyebrows, dividers, labels) should encode something true about the content instead of decorating it. Many generic designs use numbered markers (01 / 02 / 03), but those fit only if the content actually is a sequence, such as a real process or a typed timeline where the order is information the reader needs. Before adding numbered markers or similar devices, check that they actually make sense.

**When the page is a UI (dashboard, tool).** It is scanned and operated instead of read top to bottom, so the craft shifts from typography to information design. Put the summary before the detail. Encode state in form as well as in numbers (a pill, a chip, a severity stripe) so that whatever needs attention is visible at a glance. Semantic color (good / warning / critical) is separate from the accent hue and doesn't count as your accent. Give sparklines and charts the same care as type: an area fill, a faint grid, an emphasized endpoint. Interactive elements should look interactive.



## Process

Start from what the viewer should be able to do on the page, in addition to what they will read. If the page should take input, keep what people change for whoever opens it next, show live data, or ask Claude something, load the `artifact-capabilities` skill now and design around what it makes available to this user. A page that is only read doesn't need that.

Before writing code, sketch a short design plan (a compact token system with color, type, and layout):
- **Color**: describe the palette as 4-6 named hex values.
- **Type**: typefaces for 2+ roles: a characterful display face used with restraint, a complementary body face, and a utility face for captions or data if needed.
- **Layout**: a layout concept in one or two sentences.

Then build, following the plan and deriving every color and type decision from it.

**Write, look once, publish.** Before publishing you may look at the rendered page once: one screenshot of the local file, or the `ArtifactCheck` tool's preview (or the Artifact tool's own `action: "preview"` where there is no separate `ArtifactCheck` tool) where this session offers it. Then make one pass of edits for what it shows, without a second look. For a page that charts real numbers, do take that look instead of skipping it, and use it on the chart. Don't build a test loop around your own file: no repeated screenshots, no pulling the script out to run it through node, no scripts that probe the DOM. Such a loop spends the session re-checking what a careful write already got right, while the user waits for a link. Then publish. A page whose point is logic or stored data takes its one check here, not in a render loop: exercise once any `window.claude` call that the preview couldn't run (read the stored data back, for example), and stop. Review happens on the live page, and further polish is for the user to request. That check is for runtime code you wrote into this page, not for content you fill into an Artifact made from an Artifact type (a Slides deck, a Design canvas): there the type's own instructions say whether to check, and if they say nothing, don't. If the user reports something visibly broken (a clipped column, unreadable text, a control that does nothing), fix that and republish once.

**Open viewers.** You don't need to do anything for viewers who already have the page open: published changes are delivered to them automatically at their next quiet moment, with state preserved where possible. If your page has state a viewer would miss (a game, a long form), register `window.claude?.hot?.snapshot(...)` and boot through `window.claude?.hot?.ready ? window.claude.hot.ready(start) : start(window.claude?.hot?.data ?? {})`.

## When the request is editorial

The stance changes here: the client has already rejected proposals that felt templated, and is paying for a distinctive point of view. Make opinionated decisions, and take one real aesthetic risk where it serves the work.

Review the design plan against the subject before building: if any part of it reads like the generic default you would produce for any similar page, revise that part, and note what you changed and why. Write the code only after confirming the plan is unique, following the revised plan exactly.

**Principles** 

- The hero states the thesis: open with the most characteristic thing in the subject's world (headline, image, live demo, interactive moment). 
- Typography sets the personality of the page. Pair the display and body faces deliberately, avoiding the families you would use on any other project, and set a clear type scale with intentional weights, widths, and spacing. Make the type treatment itself a memorable part of the design instead of a neutral container for the content. 
- Use motion deliberately. Think about whether and where animation can serve the subject: a page-load sequence, hover micro-interactions, ambient atmosphere. One orchestrated moment is usually more effective than scattered effects; choose what the direction calls for. However, sometimes less is more, and extra animation adds to the impression that the design is AI-generated. 
- Match complexity to the vision. Maximalist directions need elaborate execution; minimal directions need precision in spacing, type, and detail. Elegance is executing the chosen vision well.
- Put your boldness in one place; keep everything around it quiet. If the accent clashes with the background, shift it toward an analogous hue or desaturate it instead of replacing it.

Platform-native UI - use BlueprintJS 3 components and Tailwind CSS.

content.content:
1	# Decisions: what the code does today
2	
3	Worktree: `/mnt/data/projects/discourse-graph/.claude/worktrees/push-pull-repros` at `b3796a70`. Read-only, and all paths are relative to the worktree. Line numbers are real at this commit. None of the cited ranges had drifted.
4	
5	## Summary
6	
7	| # | Case | Verdict | Code today (one line) |
8	|---|---|---|---|
9	| 1 | PUB-04 | CONFIRMED | Unchecking a pre-checked group only leaves it out of this publish. The existing grants stay, and neither app has an unshare action. |
10	| 2 | PUB-11 | CONFIRMED (broader) | The warning only checks that the Source exists in this space's DB. It never checks whether the target group can see the Source. |
11	| 3 | DSC-06 | CONFIRMED | Grants are keyed to the group. No code or trigger removes them when a member leaves or a space's access is removed. |
12	| 4 | TXT-04 | PARTLY | Wikilinks and tags reach Roam's `fromMarkdown` unchanged. Whether pages get created is Roam's behavior, and `[[a\|b]]` is never translated. |
13	| 5 | TXT-06 | CONFIRMED | Refresh appends new blocks and then deletes every old top-level block and its children. The page uid survives; block uids don't. |
14	| 6 | TTL-11 | CONFIRMED | Both decorate to `[[CLM]] - Sleep helps`, and the second import fails with "A page titled … already exists …". |
15	| 7 | TTL-15 | CONFIRMED | Sync silently skips titles that match no format. Cleanup keys on uid existence, so the last version stays shared. |
16	| 8 | AST-06 | CONFIRMED | Only the metadata cache's `embeds` get uploaded. A plain link reaches the destination as a dead link. |
17	| 9 | AST-08 | PARTLY | The path is only relative when the asset sits under the note's folder. Otherwise the asset keeps its full source vault path under `import/<space>/`. |
18	| 10 | UPD-09 | CONFIRMED | Imported nodes are hidden in both apps. The only way to update is a manual Refresh button or a refresh-all command, with no stale indicator. |
19	| 11 | DEL-03 | PARTLY | There is no unshare path. But leaving the group does *not* stop sharing, and deleting the node does remove its grants (DB trigger). |
20	| 12 | REL-05 | PARTLY | Removal leaves no record, so the relation comes back. Scope is wider in Roam (any dialog import, any space), and Obsidian's pending rows have no delete button. |
21	| 13 | REL-07 | CONFIRMED | Roam Refresh never imports relations. Obsidian Refresh *does* import relations for the whole source space. |
22	| 14 | REL-08 | CONFIRMED | Roam sync has no relation step. Obsidian publishes a relation when it is created and reconciles relation grants on every full sync. |
23	| 15 | REL-09 | CONFIRMED | The source deletes the relation's Concept at cleanup, and a trigger drops its grants. Destinations never delete their copies. |
24	| 16 | SEC-03 | CONFIRMED | Delete policy: `in_space(space_id,'editor') OR can_access_account(account_uid)`. Any member of the grantee group qualifies. |
25	| 17 | SEC-04 | CONFIRMED | The views need SpaceAccess. Table SELECT policies and `file_access` need only ResourceAccess. |
26	
27	---
28	
29	## 1. PUB-04: unchecking an already-shared group
30	
31	**Verdict: CONFIRMED**
32	
33	**Code today.** In Roam's publish dialog a group starts checked only when *every* selected node is already shared with it. Unchecking it just removes it from this publish, because publishing only upserts grants (`ignoreDuplicates`) and never deletes them. With every group unchecked, Publish is disabled. In Obsidian, already-shared groups show a ✓. They are a no-op in the suggest modal and disabled in the dropdown ("Already published to this group").
34	
35	**Evidence**
36	- `apps/roam/src/components/Export.tsx:837-846` sets `preselectedGroupIds` from groups where `publishableNodes.every(({ uid }) => publishedIdsByGroup[id].has(uid))`. Then `setSelectedGroupIds(preselectedGroupIds);`.
37	- `apps/roam/src/components/Export.tsx:1257-1260`: `checked ? [...prev, group.id] : prev.filter((id) => id !== group.id)`
38	- `apps/roam/src/components/Export.tsx:1286-1290`: `disabled={ loading || selectedGroupIds.length === 0 || publishableNodes.length === 0 }`
39	- `apps/roam/src/utils/publishNodesToGroups.ts:468-470`: `.from("ResourceAccess") .upsert(resourceAccesses, { ignoreDuplicates: true });`
40	- `apps/obsidian/src/components/PublishGroupSuggestModal.tsx:25`: `` return item.isPublished ? `${item.name} (shared)` : item.name; ``
41	- `apps/obsidian/src/components/PublishGroupSuggestModal.tsx:54-57`: `onChooseSuggestion(item) { if (item.isPublished) { return; } ...`
42	- `apps/obsidian/src/components/PublishGroupDropdown.tsx:214, 221-224`: `disabled={isPublishing || group.isPublished}`, title `"Already published to this group"`
43	- `apps/obsidian/src/utils/publishGroupSelection.ts:97-99`: `if (publishedToGroups.includes(groupId)) { throw new Error("Already shared with this group"); }`
44	
45	**Note**
46	- Roam: when only some of the selected nodes are shared with a group, it shows unchecked, so the dialog can't show partial sharing.
47	- Obsidian's "shared" state comes from the note's `publishedToGroups` frontmatter (`publishNode.ts:27-33`), not from the DB.
48	- Hidden side effect in Obsidian: if a user hand-deletes a group from `publishedToGroups`, the next full sync deletes that group's grants for *relations* touching the note (`publishNode.ts:358-369`, `ensurePublishedRelationsAccuracy`). The node's own grant stays. This is the only code path that ever deletes a ResourceAccess row (see item 11).
49	- The Roam page-title "Publish" button opens the same Export dialog (`openShareNodeDialog.ts:12-16`).
50	
51	## 2. PUB-11: Evidence published while its Source isn't shared
52	
53	**Verdict: CONFIRMED, and broader than the claim**
54	
55	**Code today.** Roam only warns when the Source is neither in the same publish batch nor present in this space's `my_concepts`. It never checks whether the target group can see the Source. With suggestive mode on, Roam syncs every node, so the Source is always present and no warning ever shows.
56	
57	**Evidence**
58	- `apps/roam/src/utils/publishNodesToGroups.ts:346-360`: the check is `sourceId === undefined || isRid(sourceId) || nodesByUid.has(sourceId) || syncedUids.has(sourceId)`, and then `return node;`. Otherwise it shows the toast: `Source "…" is not in this space yet. Publishing without this source reference. …`
59	- `publishNodesToGroups.ts:326-330`: `syncedUids` is `from("my_concepts")…eq("space_id", spaceId).in("source_local_id", neededUids)`, with no group filter.
60	- `apps/roam/src/utils/syncDgNodesToSupabase.ts:1270`: `const sharedNodesOnlySync = !isSyncEnabled();`
61	- `syncDgNodesToSupabase.ts:1440-1444`: `nodeInstancesToSync = sharedNodesOnlySync ? nonImportedNodeInstances.filter(… sharedSourceLocalIds.has …) : nonImportedNodeInstances;`
62	- `apps/roam/src/components/settings/utils/accessors.ts:764-765`: `isSyncEnabled = () => getFeatureFlag("Suggestive mode overlay enabled")`
63	
64	**Note**
65	- The warning is also skipped with suggestive mode off, whenever the Source was ever published to *any* group. That publish puts the Source in `my_concepts`, but the new group still can't see it.
66	- A Source that is itself imported (a RID slot value) never warns.
67	- The Roam destination then titles the page with the missing-source placeholder. It warns: `Its source (…) is not in this graph. Import the source, then refresh this page.` (`materializeSharedNode.ts:153-156`). The user can't act on that, because the Source isn't shared with them.
68	- Obsidian runs the same existence-only check (`sourceSlot.ts:169-201`, RPC `rid_or_local_id_to_concept_db_id`) and only writes a `console.warn`, with no user-visible warning.
69	
70	## 3. DSC-06: source space leaves the group
71	
72	**Verdict: CONFIRMED**
73	
74	**Code today.** Grants (`ResourceAccess.account_uid`) name the group, and nothing deletes them or the group's `SpaceAccess` row when a member leaves. The "leave group" action (website) deletes only the `group_membership` row, and that table has no trigger. Remaining members keep satisfying the view condition, so the node stays visible. The source user is still an editor of their own space and keeps syncing the node, so the node keeps updating.
75	
76	**Evidence**
77	- `packages/database/supabase/schemas/content.sql:164-168`: `ResourceAccess (account_uid UUID, space_id bigint, source_local_id …)`.
78	- `content.sql:183-185`: FK `account_uid` → `auth.users(id) … ON DELETE CASCADE`. This cascade only fires when the group account itself is deleted.
79	- `content.sql:277-281` (`my_contents`) and `packages/database/supabase/schemas/concept.sql:195-199` (`my_concepts`): `space_id = any(my_space_ids('reader')) OR (space_id = any(my_space_ids('partial')) AND ra.space_id IS NOT NULL)`.
80	- `packages/database/supabase/schemas/account.sql:216-223`: `my_user_accounts()` returns `auth.uid()` plus the `group_id`s from `group_membership`.
81	- `apps/website/app/utils/supabase/account.ts:150-155`: `.from("group_membership").delete().eq("member_id", memberId).eq("group_id", groupId)`.
82	- Every place that removes ResourceAccess rows:
83	  - `concept.sql:633-648`: when the last Content/Concept/Document for an id is deleted.
84	  - `concept.sql:669-680`: when a Space is deleted.
85	  - The FK cascade when the group account is deleted.
86	  - `apps/obsidian/src/utils/publishNode.ts:363-368`: relation grants only.
87	- No app code deletes `SpaceAccess`. The only ResourceAccess `.delete()` in app code is at `publishNode.ts:364`.
88	
89	**Note.** There is no "space leaves a group" operation as such. A space is linked to a group only by `SpaceAccess(group, space, 'partial')`, and no UI removes that row. A source editor could remove it by hand (`account.sql:534`, editor-only), which leads to item 17.
90	
91	## 4. TXT-04: Obsidian wikilinks and tags into Roam
92	
93	**Verdict: PARTLY**
94	
95	**Code today.** The only processing on the import path is:
96	1. Strip frontmatter.
97	2. Rewrite links whose locator matches a `FileReference` row.
98	3. Protect `{{pdf: url}}`.
99	
100	Everything else reaches Roam's `page.fromMarkdown` / `block.fromMarkdown` verbatim. So `[[link]]`, `[[link|alias]]` and `#tag` arrive as literal text, and Roam's own parser turns them into page references. `[[link|alias]]` is not translated into Roam alias syntax, so it can only reference a page literally named `link|alias`.
101	
102	**Evidence**
103	- `apps/roam/src/utils/rewriteAssetLinks.ts:295-296`: "The wikilink branches match Roam page references too, but those never resolve: a page name is not a recorded locator."
104	- `rewriteAssetLinks.ts:317`: `\[\[([^\]|\n]+)(?:\|([^\]\n]*))?\]\]` matches, but line 459 leaves it alone: `if (matched === undefined) return match;`
105	- `apps/roam/src/utils/materializeSharedNode.ts:225-229`: `stripFrontmatter(data.text)`, then `trimBlankLines`.
106	- `materializeSharedNode.ts:276-279` / `341-344`: `fromMarkdown({ … "markdown-string": protectMediaEmbeds(markdown) })`.
107	- `apps/roam/src/utils/protectMediaEmbeds.ts:45-49` touches only `{{pdf|audio|video|iframe|youtube: url}}`.
108	
109	**Note.** Whether Roam creates empty pages for these references, and how it parses `|` inside `[[…]]`, is Roam's runtime behavior and not in the repo, so that part is UNSETTLED from code. `![[Some note]]` (a note embed rather than an asset) also passes through as literal text. The one exception: a `[[doc.pdf]]` whose file is also embedded in the same note has a row and gets rewritten to the copied asset.
110	
111	## 5. TXT-06: Refresh and block ids
112	
113	**Verdict: CONFIRMED**
114	
115	**Code today.** Updating an imported page works like this:
116	1. Read the page's current top-level children.
117	2. Append the fresh markdown as new blocks, which get new uids.
118	3. Delete every old top-level block. Deleting a block also deletes its children.
119	
120	Anything the user added on the page, at any depth, is deleted, and `((block refs))` into the old blocks point to deleted uids. The page uid itself survives (renames go through `updatePage`), so page references keep working.
121	
122	**Evidence**
123	- `apps/roam/src/utils/materializeSharedNode.ts:338-346`: `const previousChildren = getShallowTreeByParentUid(pageUid); if (markdown) { await getRoamMarkdownApi().block.fromMarkdown({ location: { "parent-uid": pageUid, order: "last" }, … }); } await Promise.all(previousChildren.map(({ uid }) => deleteBlock(uid)));`
124	- `materializeSharedNode.ts:359`: `window.roamAlphaAPI.updatePage({ page: { uid: pageUid, title } })`
125	- `apps/roam/src/components/RefreshImportedNodeTitleButton.tsx:21`: `refreshImportedNode({ pageUid: uid, force: true })`
126	- `apps/roam/src/utils/refreshAllImportedNodes.ts:21`: `refreshImportedNode({ pageUid, force: false })`
127	
128	**Note**
129	- The page-title Refresh button always forces, so every click wipes and rewrites the page even when the source hasn't changed.
130	- "DG: Refresh all imported nodes" skips pages that are up to date (`materializeSharedNode.ts:431-445`).
131	- A first-time import that hits an existing page fails instead of overwriting it (item 6).
132	- How Roam renders a dangling `((uid))` is Roam runtime behavior.
133	
134	## 6. TTL-11: same claim from two spaces into one Roam graph
135	
136	**Verdict: CONFIRMED**, provided both shared nodes resolve to the same local node type
137	
138	**Code today.** The page title is `decorateTitle(localFormat, coreTitle)`, so the Obsidian `CLM - Sleep helps` and the Roam `[[CLM]] - Sleep helps` both become `[[CLM]] - Sleep helps`. The second import has no page linked to its RID, finds a page with that title, and fails at stage `title-collision`. The import dialog summary shows it under "N failed" as `<shared title>: <message>`. The failed row stays selected.
139	
140	**Message the user gets**
141	> `A page titled "[[CLM]] - Sleep helps" already exists and was not imported from "<sourceNodeRid>". Rename or remove that page, then import again`
142	
143	The raw RID is shown as-is.
144	
145	**Evidence**
146	- `apps/roam/src/utils/materializeSharedNode.ts:171-176`: `const coreTitle = sharedNode.coreTitle; if (!coreTitle || !nodeType) return { title: incomingTitle }; … decorateTitle(nodeType.format, coreTitle) ?? incomingTitle`
147	- `materializeSharedNode.ts:242-249`: `if (!importedPageUid) return getPageUidByPageTitle(title) ? failure({ … message: \`A page titled "${title}" already exists and was not imported from "${identity.sourceNodeRid}". Rename or remove that page, then import again\`, stage: "title-collision" }) : undefined;`
148	- `apps/roam/src/components/DiscoverSharedNodesDialog.tsx:177-181`: failed items render as `{item.sharedNode.title}: {item.message}`.
149	- `DiscoverSharedNodesDialog.tsx:323-325`: failed RIDs stay selected.
150	
151	**Note**
152	- The list itself does tell the two apart: the "Source space" column shows the space name and URI (`DiscoverSharedNodesDialog.tsx:66-80`).
153	- The workaround isn't stable. If the user renames the first page, the second import succeeds. But the next forced or changed Refresh of the first page tries to rename it back, and fails with `Cannot rename the imported page "…" to "…": another page already has that title…` (`materializeSharedNode.ts:251-258`).
154	- A native local page with that title blocks the import the same way.
155	
156	## 7. TTL-15: Roam node renamed so no format matches
157	
158	**Verdict: CONFIRMED**
159	
160	**Code today.** The sync drops a shared node whose current title matches no node-type format, and no toast appears. Orphan cleanup deletes DB rows only when the Roam uid no longer exists. A renamed page keeps its uid, so its last-synced Concept, Content and grants stay in the DB, and destinations can still import or refresh that old version. Deleting the page is the only way the grants go away (item 11).
161	
162	**Evidence**
163	- `apps/roam/src/utils/syncDgNodesToSupabase.ts:1170-1176`: `const matchingNodeType = typeMatchers.find(({ regex }) => regex.test(row.text))?.node; if (matchingNodeType === undefined) { return []; }`
164	- `apps/roam/src/utils/cleanupOrphanedNodes.ts:145-150`: `[:find ?uid :in $ [?uid ...] :where (not [_ :block/uid ?uid])]`
165	- `cleanupOrphanedNodes.ts:389-398`: only the uids returned by that query are deleted.
166	- `syncDgNodesToSupabase.ts:914-931`: the `orphaned` count from the core-title backfill goes only to `posthog.capture`. There is no toast.
167	
168	**Note.** The publish dialog lists only nodes that are currently discourse nodes, so the renamed page can't be republished or managed from there. Renaming it back to a matching title resumes updates.
169	
170	## 8. AST-06: linked, not embedded, Obsidian files
171	
172	**Verdict: CONFIRMED**
173	
174	**Code today.** Obsidian collects assets only from the metadata cache's `embeds` (`![[…]]` / `![](…)`). A `[[doc.pdf]]` or `[doc](doc.pdf)` link is in `links`, not `embeds`, so the file is never uploaded and gets no `FileReference` row.
175	
176	**What the destination sees**
177	- **Roam**: the text arrives as written, because the rewrite skips locators with no row. `[[doc.pdf]]` becomes a Roam page reference to `doc.pdf`, and `[doc](doc.pdf)` a relative link that leads nowhere.
178	- **Obsidian**: the link is rewritten to a dead link under the import folder, e.g. `[[import/<space>/…/doc.pdf|doc.pdf]]`. If the user creates it, the file lands there.
179	
180	**Evidence**
181	- `apps/obsidian/src/utils/syncDgNodesToSupabase.ts:765`: `const embeds = plugin.app.metadataCache.getFileCache(file)?.embeds ?? [];`
182	- `syncDgNodesToSupabase.ts:767-775`: resolves each embed and drops links that resolve to nothing.
183	- `apps/obsidian/src/utils/publishNode.ts:445`: publish uses `findEmbeddedAttachments`.
184	- `apps/roam/src/utils/rewriteAssetLinks.ts:459`: `if (matched === undefined) return match;`
185	- `apps/obsidian/src/utils/importNodes.ts:655-663`: "Unresolved (dead) link from another vault: rewrite so that when the user creates the file from this link, it is created under import/{vaultName}/…", then `` return `${importFolder}/${canonicalSourcePath}`; ``
186	
187	**Note.** Exception: when the same file is *also* embedded somewhere in that note, it does have a row, and both apps rewrite the plain link to the copied asset too. On a Roam destination, the "creates an empty page" part is Roam runtime behavior (see item 4).
188	
189	## 9. AST-08: where assets land in Obsidian
190	
191	**Verdict: PARTLY**
192	
193	**Code today.** The target path is `<space import folder>/<path>`. `<path>` is relative to the source note's folder only when the asset sits inside that folder. Otherwise it is the asset's full source vault path. Other special cases:
194	- If this vault already imported the same file hash, and that copy still exists, the old path is reused.
195	- A name that sanitizes to nothing becomes `asset-<hash8>`.
196	- The space folder is `import/<sanitized space name>`, found by space URI, and gets a `-<shortId>` suffix on a name clash.
197	
198	**Evidence**
199	- `apps/obsidian/src/utils/importNodes.ts:990-1006`: `const localPath = sourcePath ?? filepath; const pathForImport = originalNodePath !== undefined ? getAssetPathRelativeToNote(localPath, originalNodePath) : localPath; … const candidatePath = \`${importBasePath}/${sanitizedAssetPath || \`asset-${filehash.slice(0, 8)}\`}\`;`

# Decisions: what the code does today

Worktree: `/mnt/data/projects/discourse-graph/.claude/worktrees/push-pull-repros` at `b3796a70`. Read-only, and all paths are relative to the worktree. Line numbers are real at this commit. None of the cited ranges had drifted.

## Summary

| # | Case | Verdict | Code today (one line) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | PUB-04 | CONFIRMED | Unchecking a pre-checked group only leaves it out of this publish. The existing grants stay, and neither app has an unshare action. |
| 2 | PUB-11 | CONFIRMED (broader) | The warning only checks that the Source exists in this space's DB. It never checks whether the target group can see the Source. |
| 3 | DSC-06 | CONFIRMED | Grants are keyed to the group. No code or trigger removes them when a member leaves or a space's access is removed. |
| 4 | TXT-04 | PARTLY | Wikilinks and tags reach Roam's `fromMarkdown` unchanged. Whether pages get created is Roam's behavior, and `[[a\|b]]` is never translated. |
| 5 | TXT-06 | CONFIRMED | Refresh appends new blocks and then deletes every old top-level block and its children. The page uid survives; block uids don't. |
| 6 | TTL-11 | CONFIRMED | Both decorate to `[[CLM]] - Sleep helps`, and the second import fails with "A page titled … already exists …". |
| 7 | TTL-15 | CONFIRMED | Sync silently skips titles that match no format. Cleanup keys on uid existence, so the last version stays shared. |
| 8 | AST-06 | CONFIRMED | Only the metadata cache's `embeds` get uploaded. A plain link reaches the destination as a dead link. |
| 9 | AST-08 | PARTLY | The path is only relative when the asset sits under the note's folder. Otherwise the asset keeps its full source vault path under `import/<space>/`. |
| 10 | UPD-09 | CONFIRMED | Imported nodes are hidden in both apps. The only way to update is a manual Refresh button or a refresh-all command, with no stale indicator. |
| 11 | DEL-03 | PARTLY | There is no unshare path. But leaving the group does *not* stop sharing, and deleting the node does remove its grants (DB trigger). |
| 12 | REL-05 | PARTLY | Removal leaves no record, so the relation comes back. Scope is wider in Roam (any dialog import, any space), and Obsidian's pending rows have no delete button. |
| 13 | REL-07 | CONFIRMED | Roam Refresh never imports relations. Obsidian Refresh *does* import relations for the whole source space. |
| 14 | REL-08 | CONFIRMED | Roam sync has no relation step. Obsidian publishes a relation when it is created and reconciles relation grants on every full sync. |
| 15 | REL-09 | CONFIRMED | The source deletes the relation's Concept at cleanup, and a trigger drops its grants. Destinations never delete their copies. |
| 16 | SEC-03 | CONFIRMED | Delete policy: `in_space(space_id,'editor') OR can_access_account(account_uid)`. Any member of the grantee group qualifies. |
| 17 | SEC-04 | CONFIRMED | The views need SpaceAccess. Table SELECT policies and `file_access` need only ResourceAccess. |

---

## 1. PUB-04: unchecking an already-shared group

**Verdict: CONFIRMED**

**Code today.** In Roam's publish dialog a group starts checked only when *every* selected node is already shared with it. Unchecking it just removes it from this publish, because publishing only upserts grants (`ignoreDuplicates`) and never deletes them. With every group unchecked, Publish is disabled. In Obsidian, already-shared groups show a ✓. They are a no-op in the suggest modal and disabled in the dropdown ("Already published to this group").

**Evidence**
- `apps/roam/src/components/Export.tsx:837-846` sets `preselectedGroupIds` from groups where `publishableNodes.every(({ uid }) => publishedIdsByGroup[id].has(uid))`. Then `setSelectedGroupIds(preselectedGroupIds);`.
- `apps/roam/src/components/Export.tsx:1257-1260`: `checked ? [...prev, group.id] : prev.filter((id) => id !== group.id)`
- `apps/roam/src/components/Export.tsx:1286-1290`: `disabled={ loading || selectedGroupIds.length === 0 || publishableNodes.length === 0 }`
- `apps/roam/src/utils/publishNodesToGroups.ts:468-470`: `.from("ResourceAccess") .upsert(resourceAccesses, { ignoreDuplicates: true });`
- `apps/obsidian/src/components/PublishGroupSuggestModal.tsx:25`: `` return item.isPublished ? `${item.name} (shared)` : item.name; ``
- `apps/obsidian/src/components/PublishGroupSuggestModal.tsx:54-57`: `onChooseSuggestion(item) { if (item.isPublished) { return; } ...`
- `apps/obsidian/src/components/PublishGroupDropdown.tsx:214, 221-224`: `disabled={isPublishing || group.isPublished}`, title `"Already published to this group"`
- `apps/obsidian/src/utils/publishGroupSelection.ts:97-99`: `if (publishedToGroups.includes(groupId)) { throw new Error("Already shared with this group"); }`

**Note**
- Roam: when only some of the selected nodes are shared with a group, it shows unchecked, so the dialog can't show partial sharing.
- Obsidian's "shared" state comes from the note's `publishedToGroups` frontmatter (`publishNode.ts:27-33`), not from the DB.
- Hidden side effect in Obsidian: if a user hand-deletes a group from `publishedToGroups`, the next full sync deletes that group's grants for *relations* touching the note (`publishNode.ts:358-369`, `ensurePublishedRelationsAccuracy`). The node's own grant stays. This is the only code path that ever deletes a ResourceAccess row (see item 11).
- The Roam page-title "Publish" button opens the same Export dialog (`openShareNodeDialog.ts:12-16`).

## 2. PUB-11: Evidence published while its Source isn't shared

**Verdict: CONFIRMED, and broader than the claim**

**Code today.** Roam only warns when the Source is neither in the same publish batch nor present in this space's `my_concepts`. It never checks whether the target group can see the Source. With suggestive mode on, Roam syncs every node, so the Source is always present and no warning ever shows.

**Evidence**
- `apps/roam/src/utils/publishNodesToGroups.ts:346-360`: the check is `sourceId === undefined || isRid(sourceId) || nodesByUid.has(sourceId) || syncedUids.has(sourceId)`, and then `return node;`. Otherwise it shows the toast: `Source "…" is not in this space yet. Publishing without this source reference. …`
- `publishNodesToGroups.ts:326-330`: `syncedUids` is `from("my_concepts")…eq("space_id", spaceId).in("source_local_id", neededUids)`, with no group filter.
- `apps/roam/src/utils/syncDgNodesToSupabase.ts:1270`: `const sharedNodesOnlySync = !isSyncEnabled();`
- `syncDgNodesToSupabase.ts:1440-1444`: `nodeInstancesToSync = sharedNodesOnlySync ? nonImportedNodeInstances.filter(… sharedSourceLocalIds.has …) : nonImportedNodeInstances;`
- `apps/roam/src/components/settings/utils/accessors.ts:764-765`: `isSyncEnabled = () => getFeatureFlag("Suggestive mode overlay enabled")`

**Note**
- The warning is also skipped with suggestive mode off, whenever the Source was ever published to *any* group. That publish puts the Source in `my_concepts`, but the new group still can't see it.
- A Source that is itself imported (a RID slot value) never warns.
- The Roam destination then titles the page with the missing-source placeholder. It warns: `Its source (…) is not in this graph. Import the source, then refresh this page.` (`materializeSharedNode.ts:153-156`). The user can't act on that, because the Source isn't shared with them.
- Obsidian runs the same existence-only check (`sourceSlot.ts:169-201`, RPC `rid_or_local_id_to_concept_db_id`) and only writes a `console.warn`, with no user-visible warning.

## 3. DSC-06: source space leaves the group

**Verdict: CONFIRMED**

**Code today.** Grants (`ResourceAccess.account_uid`) name the group, and nothing deletes them or the group's `SpaceAccess` row when a member leaves. The "leave group" action (website) deletes only the `group_membership` row, and that table has no trigger. Remaining members keep satisfying the view condition, so the node stays visible. The source user is still an editor of their own space and keeps syncing the node, so the node keeps updating.

**Evidence**
- `packages/database/supabase/schemas/content.sql:164-168`: `ResourceAccess (account_uid UUID, space_id bigint, source_local_id …)`.
- `content.sql:183-185`: FK `account_uid` → `auth.users(id) … ON DELETE CASCADE`. This cascade only fires when the group account itself is deleted.
- `content.sql:277-281` (`my_contents`) and `packages/database/supabase/schemas/concept.sql:195-199` (`my_concepts`): `space_id = any(my_space_ids('reader')) OR (space_id = any(my_space_ids('partial')) AND ra.space_id IS NOT NULL)`.
- `packages/database/supabase/schemas/account.sql:216-223`: `my_user_accounts()` returns `auth.uid()` plus the `group_id`s from `group_membership`.
- `apps/website/app/utils/supabase/account.ts:150-155`: `.from("group_membership").delete().eq("member_id", memberId).eq("group_id", groupId)`.
- Every place that removes ResourceAccess rows:
  - `concept.sql:633-648`: when the last Content/Concept/Document for an id is deleted.
  - `concept.sql:669-680`: when a Space is deleted.
  - The FK cascade when the group account is deleted.
  - `apps/obsidian/src/utils/publishNode.ts:363-368`: relation grants only.
- No app code deletes `SpaceAccess`. The only ResourceAccess `.delete()` in app code is at `publishNode.ts:364`.

**Note.** There is no "space leaves a group" operation as such. A space is linked to a group only by `SpaceAccess(group, space, 'partial')`, and no UI removes that row. A source editor could remove it by hand (`account.sql:534`, editor-only), which leads to item 17.

## 4. TXT-04: Obsidian wikilinks and tags into Roam

**Verdict: PARTLY**

**Code today.** The only processing on the import path is:
1. Strip frontmatter.
2. Rewrite links whose locator matches a `FileReference` row.
3. Protect `{{pdf: url}}`.

Everything else reaches Roam's `page.fromMarkdown` / `block.fromMarkdown` verbatim. So `[[link]]`, `[[link|alias]]` and `#tag` arrive as literal text, and Roam's own parser turns them into page references. `[[link|alias]]` is not translated into Roam alias syntax, so it can only reference a page literally named `link|alias`.

**Evidence**
- `apps/roam/src/utils/rewriteAssetLinks.ts:295-296`: "The wikilink branches match Roam page references too, but those never resolve: a page name is not a recorded locator."
- `rewriteAssetLinks.ts:317`: `\[\[([^\]|\n]+)(?:\|([^\]\n]*))?\]\]` matches, but line 459 leaves it alone: `if (matched === undefined) return match;`
- `apps/roam/src/utils/materializeSharedNode.ts:225-229`: `stripFrontmatter(data.text)`, then `trimBlankLines`.
- `materializeSharedNode.ts:276-279` / `341-344`: `fromMarkdown({ … "markdown-string": protectMediaEmbeds(markdown) })`.
- `apps/roam/src/utils/protectMediaEmbeds.ts:45-49` touches only `{{pdf|audio|video|iframe|youtube: url}}`.

**Note.** Whether Roam creates empty pages for these references, and how it parses `|` inside `[[…]]`, is Roam's runtime behavior and not in the repo, so that part is UNSETTLED from code. `![[Some note]]` (a note embed rather than an asset) also passes through as literal text. The one exception: a `[[doc.pdf]]` whose file is also embedded in the same note has a row and gets rewritten to the copied asset.

## 5. TXT-06: Refresh and block ids

**Verdict: CONFIRMED**

I'm settling on the format for each entry: an ID/question header, options listed, current code behavior, and a recommended default with a brief justification, keeping recommendations aligned with Sid's MVP-0 philosophy — ship minimal but safe, documenting known gaps rather than over-building.

I'm drafting the first entry now, on whether there's any way to unshare a node in v0, weighing the option of no unshare support versus allowing unchecking already-shared groups to revoke access versus a dedicated stop-sharing action.

Looking at current behavior: Roam only pre-checks a group when all selected nodes are shared with it, and unchecking just excludes it from that publish rather than revoking anything, since publish only adds grants — Obsidian works similarly, showing shared groups as checked but non-actionable. Neither app supports true unsharing; deletion cleans up grants via a trigger, but leaving a group or renaming a node out of format doesn't, and in Obsidian, manually editing publishedToGroups only affects relation grants on the next sync. I'm leaning toward recommending option (a) for v0 — treat unsharing as a known gap, mirror the checked-and-disabled pattern for already-shared groups so the dialog doesn't promise something it can't do, and rely on node deletion as the sanctioned way out, since real revocation touches grants, relations, and destination copies in ways too broad for v0. I'm noting though that making groups disabled in Roam's UI is itself a small code change, so the expected behavior description should probably read "already-shared groups are checked and can't be unchecked."

Now I'm moving to the second question about whether publish should warn when a Source exists in the database but isn't visible to the target group. I'm reviewing how the existing warning works — it only fires when the Source is missing entirely from the space's database, which means it silently never fires in suggestive mode and stops firing once a Source has been published anywhere, leaving imported Sources unwarned; Obsidian mirrors this with only a console log, and the destination ends up showing an unhelpful placeholder message telling the user to do something they can't. I'm settling on recommending option (a): warn whenever any target group lacks visibility into the Source, based on actual grants rather than existence, and name the Source explicitly in the warning.

Next I'm considering whether a space leaving a group should keep its nodes visible to the group, but first I need to clarify that there's no explicit "space leaves a group" operation in the code — group membership belongs to a space's account, so leaving just deletes that membership row while grants and access records stay intact, meaning nodes would remain visible.

Now I'm weighing three options: leaving keeps everything visible and syncing as-is (current behavior), leaving freezes the shared nodes so they stop updating, or leaving fully revokes the space's grants to that group. I lean toward thinking about user expectations here — similar to how Slack keeps past messages after someone leaves a channel, a research collaboration context suggests what was already shared should stay shared, though whether it continues updating is the open question.

Given there's no in-app leave mechanism for spaces yet (only via the website) and no unshare feature in v0, I'm recommending documenting that leaving a group doesn't unshare content — if you want to stop sharing, you delete the nodes. This stays consistent with the earlier PUB-04/DEL-03 decision, and I should note that the leaving user does lose visibility into the group's other content since their account no longer belongs to that group.

Now for TXT-04: how should Obsidian's [[links]] and #tags behave when imported into a Roam graph. Today they pass through unchanged, so Roam parses them as page references and may create empty pages for targets that don't exist — plus the aliased link syntax isn't translated, so it ends up referencing a page literally named with the pipe character. I'm leaning toward keeping this behavior as-is for now, accepting the new empty pages as a side effect.

Next I'm thinking through TXT-06: whether Roam Refresh should preserve block ids and any local edits on an imported page, or just replace the whole page each time — noting that a replace-all approach would discard local changes and could break block references.

Now I'm turning to TTL-11: when two nodes from different spaces share the same decorated title in one Roam graph, how should the second import be handled — either refuse the import with a clear message naming the conflicting space so the user can rename, or import it anyway with a disambiguating suffix.

Currently both nodes decorate to the same title when they map to the same local type, so the second import fails with an error showing the raw RID and telling the user to rename or remove the existing page — but renaming the first page as a workaround then breaks that page's next Refresh, since Refresh tries to rename it back. I'm weighing whether the smallest v0 fix is just improving the error message to show the space name instead of the raw RID, since the rename workaround still leaves users stuck either way, and considering whether a disambiguation suffix is actually necessary given Roam's requirement for unique titles.

Now I'm thinking about what should happen when a shared Roam node is renamed so its title no longer matches any node type — whether sync should treat it as unshared and remove it from the database like a deleted node, with destinations seeing "no longer shared" on refresh, or handle it some other way.

Checking today's behavior: sync silently skips it and cleanup only deletes uids that no longer exist, so the last version stays shared and can still be imported or refreshed, though the publish dialog stops listing it, and renaming back resumes updates. Deleting on rename feels too harsh, since a temporary typo could trigger a delete-and-recreate cycle within a 5-minute sync window that wipes out grants (since grants get deleted when the last reference disappears), forcing the user to republish — so I lean toward keeping the last version shared while warning the author that it no longer matches a type and isn't updating.

For v0, I'll settle on documenting this as a known gap by default, with an optional lightweight toast/notice if it's cheap to add — the testable expectation being that the last version stays shared and renaming back resumes updates.

Now moving to whether Obsidian notes that link (not embed) to files should also share those linked files, weighing embeds-only versus uploading linked files too.

Today only embeds get uploaded — a linked PDF becomes a dead reference in both Roam and Obsidian's import folder, and gets rewritten only if also embedded elsewhere. I'm leaning toward extending sharing to any linked non-markdown file (not just embeds), since the resolution machinery already exists and this covers common cases like linked research PDFs.

Next I'm considering where imported assets should actually land in the vault — whether to keep today's approach (import/<space>/ plus relative path when inside the note's folder, otherwise full source path) or always use the full source vault path under import/<space>/.

I'm leaning toward mirroring the full source vault path consistently since it keeps things predictable and avoids collisions across notes, whereas mixing two rules like today's approach creates ambiguity about where an asset actually sits relative to its note.

Since I can't verify exactly where notes land without more context, I'll recommend sticking with today's rule (a) for v0 since it's already implemented, and flagging it for Sid to confirm rather than pushing a change without evidence it's actually a problem for testers.

Now I'm thinking about whether the destination should indicate that a newer version of an imported node exists at the source -- weighing no indicator at all for v0 versus adding a "changed at source" marker on imported items.

Given the current code hides imported nodes and only supports manual and refresh-all commands with no timestamp comparison, I'm leaning toward keeping option (a) for v0, but noting that refresh-all needs to report correct counts first before that becomes the reliable path forward.

Now I'm considering whether a relation a user explicitly removed at the destination should stay removed rather than reappearing as pending on the next import, and looking at what today's "Remove relation" behavior actually does.

I'm checking the current implementation: Roam only shares a new relation when an endpoint is republished through the dialog, while Obsidian shares on creation and reconciles at full sync; Roam's destination refresh never imports relations (only dialog import does), while Obsidian's refresh imports relations for the whole space. Given that asymmetry, I'm leaning toward recommending option (a) — sharing relations whenever either endpoint is shared or refreshed, so both platforms behave consistently.

Now I'm moving to REL-09: what happens at the destination when the source deletes a relation, whether it's still pending or already accepted there.

Currently, the source only removes relations from its own database on cleanup, and destinations never remove copies on their own, so both pending and accepted stay regardless. I'll recommend that pending copies get dropped at the next import or Refresh since they haven't been reviewed yet, while accepted copies stay as the destination's own local relations since the destination already chose to keep them — moving on to SEC-03 about whether group members can delete another space's grants.

Today's delete policy lets either the source space's editors or any member of the grantee group (not just admins) remove grants, while insert/update stays editor-only. I'll recommend restricting delete to the node's own space editors, matching the insert rule, and pushing group-admin-based removal to a later feature — then moving to SEC-04, whether revoking a group's SpaceAccess on a space also revokes reads through that group's existing per-node grants.

Looking at the current behavior: views need SpaceAccess plus a grant, but table-level SELECT policies and storage file_access accept a grant alone, with no trigger cleaning up grants when SpaceAccess is removed, and some app paths bypass views entirely by reading tables directly. I'm leaning toward either treating SpaceAccess removal as fully revoking access, or adding a trigger that deletes the group's grants when SpaceAccess is removed, since the latter keeps the mental model simple even though it means losing grants when SpaceAccess...

Actually, I'm now favoring the approach of making table and storage reads require the same SpaceAccess condition the views enforce, so every read path agrees — this way removing SpaceAccess alone kills all reads, consistent with the expected test behavior. There's also a related interaction where leaving a group doesn't itself remove SpaceAccess, which needs to be accounted for, and I still need to check whether other P0/P1 cases remain undecided beyond the fifteen I've already covered.

I'm confirming the full list adds up to 17 P1 cases, then planning a closing section noting which cases were settled during review versus which P2 decision cases (like DSC-09, TTL-07, SCH-06, UX-09) fall outside this scope, plus flagging UX-06's unresolved count question. I'll also note that corrections to case text discovered while checking should go in the handoff doc rather than the decisions themselves, with a cross-reference between the two.

For the actual write-up, I'm keeping the style direct and concise, avoiding em dashes, and using consistent terminology throughout. Each decision gets a header formatted like "## PUB-04 and DEL-03: Is there any way to stop sharing a node in v0?" so it matches the ID-matching regex used elsewhere, and I'm double-checking that the pattern correctly captures single or paired case IDs. Now I'm ready to actually write decisions.md.
