# Open decisions for ENG-1881

Matrix revision `c601d6efba497946444fe2f9948279e035cbab3651b1371bf0754adcb03d3bdc`, candidate `b3796a70`. These are the "decide" cases at P0 and P1 that Codex's review didn't settle. Each needs an agreed expected result before its case can pass or fail. "Code today" was re-read at `b3796a70`; file references are in the case rows.

The recommended defaults are proposals, not decisions. Where a default needs a code change, the change is named so the case's expected result can be written against it.

## PUB-04 and DEL-03: Is there any way to stop sharing a node in v0?

- **Options**
  - (a) No unshare in v0. Mark it a known gap. Roam shows already-shared groups as checked and locked, as Obsidian does, so the dialog doesn't suggest an action that doesn't exist.
  - (b) Unchecking an already-shared group removes that group's grant for the node on publish.
  - (c) A separate "Stop sharing" action per node and group.
- **Code today**
  - Roam pre-checks a group only when every selected node is shared with it. Unchecking just leaves the group out of this publish, because publish only adds grants.
  - Obsidian shows shared groups with a ✓ and ignores choosing them.
  - Neither app can remove a node's grant. Deleting the node does remove its grants (cleanup, then a database trigger). Leaving the group doesn't, and neither does renaming a Roam node out of its format (TTL-15).
- **Recommended default:** (a). Revoking a grant also raises what happens to relations and to copies already imported (REL-09), which is too much for v0. Deleting the node is the documented way to stop sharing. Expected result for PUB-04: an already-shared group is checked and can't be unchecked.

## PUB-11: Should publish warn when the target group can't see the Evidence's Source?

- **Options**
  - (a) Warn whenever any target group can't see the Source, naming the Source.
  - (b) Offer to publish the Source to the same groups.
  - (c) Keep today's check and document it.
- **Code today**
  - Roam warns only when the Source isn't in this space's database at all. It never checks the target group.
  - With suggestive mode on, every node syncs, so the warning never shows. With it off, the warning stops once the Source has been published to any group. An imported Source never warns.
  - Obsidian runs the same existence check and writes only to the console.
  - The destination then shows the placeholder and says "Import the source, then refresh this page", which the user can't do because the Source isn't shared with them.
- **Recommended default:** (a). It's the smallest change that explains the placeholder the destination ends up with. Expected result: publish warns, in both suggestive modes, that the target group can't see the Source.

## DSC-06: When a space leaves a group, do its shared nodes stay visible and keep updating for the group?

- **Options**
  - (a) Yes. Leaving doesn't unshare anything (today).
  - (b) Nodes stay visible but stop updating.
  - (c) Leaving removes the space's grants to that group.
- **Code today**
  - Grants belong to the group. Leaving (website only) deletes the membership row and nothing else, so the group keeps seeing the nodes, and the source keeps syncing updates to them.
  - No app removes a space's access to a group.
- **Recommended default:** (a) for v0, documented, to stay consistent with "no unshare in v0" (PUB-04 and DEL-03). Expected result: after A leaves G, G's members still see N and its updates, and A no longer sees G's other nodes.

## TXT-04: May an imported Obsidian note's links and tags become page references in Roam?

- **Options**
  - (a) Keep `[[link]]` and `#tag` as Roam page references (today), and accept that Roam may create pages for them.
  - (b) As (a), but translate `[[Other|alias]]` into Roam's alias form, `[alias]([[Other]])`.
  - (c) Turn links whose target isn't in the graph into plain text.
- **Code today**
  - Links and tags reach Roam's markdown import unchanged, so Roam parses them as page references. Whether Roam then creates empty pages is Roam's own behavior; the case observes it.
  - `[[Other|alias]]` isn't translated, so it references a page literally named "Other|alias".
  - A linked file that is also embedded in the note is rewritten to the copied asset.
- **Recommended default:** (b). References match how Roam users write and keep the links navigable. The alias form is the one construct that produces a wrong page name. Expected result: `[[Some note]]` and `#tag` are page references, and `[[Other|alias]]` shows "alias" linked to "Other".

## TXT-06: Must Refresh keep block ids and local additions on an imported Roam page?

- **Options**
  - (a) No. Refresh replaces the page content (today). Document imported pages as copies that Refresh overwrites.
  - (b) Keep block ids where the text is unchanged.
  - (c) Keep local child blocks in a marked section that Refresh leaves alone.
- **Code today**
  - Refresh adds the new content, then deletes every old block with its children. The page uid survives. Block uids don't, so block references into the page break and local additions are deleted.
  - The title's Refresh button always forces, so each click rewrites the page even when nothing changed. Refresh-all skips unchanged pages.
- **Recommended default:** (a) for v0. UC5 says Refresh overwrites without duplicates, which this does. (b) and (c) are post-v0. Expected result: after Refresh, the page holds the source content only; references into the old blocks no longer resolve.

## TTL-11: Two nodes from two spaces decorate to the same Roam title. What happens to the second import?

- **Options**
  - (a) Refuse it (today), with a message that names the other page's source space.
  - (b) Import it under a disambiguated title, for example with the source space name appended.
  - (c) Offer to link the second node to the existing page.
- **Code today**
  - When both map to the same local type, both become "[[CLM]] - Sleep helps", and the second import fails: "A page titled … already exists and was not imported from "<raw RID>". Rename or remove that page, then import again". The raw RID is shown.
  - The import list's Source space column does tell the two apart.
  - Renaming the first page lets the second import, but the first page's next Refresh then fails trying to rename it back.
- **Recommended default:** (a) for v0, with the message naming the space instead of the raw RID. Document that one graph holds only one of two same-titled nodes; (b) is the follow-up. Expected result: the second import fails with a message naming the page and its source space, and nothing is overwritten.

## TTL-15: A shared Roam node is renamed so no node type matches. What should happen?

- **Options**
  - (a) Treat it as unshared: remove it from the database like a deleted node.
  - (b) Keep sharing the last synced version (today) and tell the author it no longer updates.
  - (c) Keep syncing it under its last known type.
- **Code today**
  - Sync skips it with no message (an analytics event only). Cleanup removes only pages that no longer exist, so the last version stays shared, and destinations can still import and refresh it.
  - The publish dialog no longer lists it. Renaming it back resumes updates.
- **Recommended default:** (b), as a known gap in v0 without the notice. (a) would drop the node's grants on a typo, and renaming back wouldn't restore them. Expected result: the last version stays shared and importable, and renaming back resumes updates.

## AST-06: Should files that an Obsidian note links to, without embedding, travel with it?

- **Options**
  - (a) Embeds only (today). Document that linked files arrive as dead links.
  - (b) Upload every linked vault file too.
  - (c) Upload linked files that aren't notes (PDFs, images, documents), the same way as embeds.
- **Code today**
  - Only embedded files are uploaded.
  - A linked `[[doc.pdf]]` becomes a Roam page reference named "doc.pdf", or a dead link under `import/<space>/` in Obsidian.
  - When the same file is also embedded in the note, the link is rewritten to the copy.
- **Recommended default:** (c). A dead link is worse than no link, research notes often link PDFs this way, and the upload path already exists for embeds. Expected result: a linked PDF opens from the destination copy. If this is too much for v0, (a) with a documented known gap is the fallback.

## AST-08: Where should imported assets land in an Obsidian vault?

- **Options**
  - (a) Today's rule, kept for v0.
  - (b) Always `import/<space>/<full source path>`.
  - (c) One attachments folder per space, or the vault's configured attachment folder.
- **Code today**
  - Assets go under `import/<space>/`. The path below that is relative to the source note's folder when the asset sits inside that folder; otherwise it is the asset's full source vault path.
  - An asset already imported with the same hash reuses its existing path. A name that sanitizes to nothing becomes `asset-<hash8>`. The space folder gets a short suffix on a name clash.
- **Recommended default:** (a). It's implemented, the last bug bash only asked the question, and no case shows harm. Revisit if testers can't find assets. Expected result: the case records the rule above, and every embed in the imported note resolves.

## UPD-09: Should a destination show that a newer version of an imported node exists?

- **Options**
  - (a) No indicator in v0 (today). Users refresh a node or run refresh-all.
  - (b) A "changed at source" marker on the imported page or note.
  - (c) List imported nodes that have updates in the import dialog, with an Update action.
- **Code today**
  - Both import lists hide nodes that are already imported, and neither app compares times.
  - Updates come only from the Refresh button on the imported page or note, and from the refresh-all commands ("DG: Refresh all imported nodes"; "Fetch latest content from imported nodes").
- **Recommended default:** (a) for v0, documented. Refresh-all is the update path, so its counts have to be right first (UPD-04). Expected result: no indicator; refresh-all brings the change.

## REL-05: Should a relation the user removed at the destination stay removed?

- **Options**
  - (a) Yes. Remember the dismissed relation and skip it on later imports.
  - (b) No. It comes back as pending (today); document it.
- **Code today**
  - Roam's "Remove relation" deletes the block and records nothing. The next dialog import of any node, from any space, re-creates it as pending. A deleted accepted relation comes back as pending too.
  - In Obsidian, pending relations have only an Accept button; only accepted ones can be deleted. The next Refresh, "Fetch latest content from imported nodes" or import from that space re-adds a deleted one as pending.
- **Recommended default:** (a). If a rejected relation returns after every import, reviewing it is pointless. Obsidian also needs a reject action on pending relations. Expected result: a removed relation doesn't return on later imports or refreshes.

## REL-07 and REL-08: When does a relation added after both nodes were shared reach a destination that already has both?

- **Options**
  - (a) Match Obsidian in both roles. A Roam source shares the relation at its next sync when both endpoints are shared to the same group. A Roam destination imports relations for the node it refreshes.
  - (b) Keep Roam as it is: the relation is shared only when an endpoint is published again, and it arrives only with a dialog import.
- **Code today**
  - Roam source: sync has no relation step, so a new relation is shared only when an endpoint is published again from the publish dialog.
  - Obsidian source: a relation is shared when it's created, for groups both endpoints are published to, and every full sync reconciles relation grants.
  - Roam destination: Refresh never imports relations. They arrive only with a dialog import, and that needs a node selected to import.
  - Obsidian destination: Refresh imports relations for the whole source space.
- **Recommended default:** (a). Obsidian is the reference flow and already does this. Expected result: after the source's next sync, a Refresh of either endpoint at the destination shows the new relation as pending.

## REL-09: The source deletes a relation that a destination has pending or accepted. What happens there?

- **Options**
  - (a) Remove pending copies at the next import or Refresh; keep accepted ones as the destination's own.
  - (b) Remove both.
  - (c) Keep both (today) and document it.
- **Code today**
  - The source removes the relation from the database at cleanup (Obsidian at full sync, Roam every sync), and a trigger drops its grants.
  - Destinations only add or update relations, so pending and accepted copies both stay.
- **Recommended default:** (a). Pending means nobody has reviewed it, so an upstream deletion should withdraw it. Accepted means the destination chose it. Expected result: the pending copy disappears at the next import or Refresh; the accepted copy stays.

## SEC-03: Can any member of a group delete the group's grants for another space's node?

- **Options**
  - (a) Only editors of the node's own space can delete its grants.
  - (b) Group admins can too.
  - (c) Any member can (today).
- **Code today:** the grant delete rule allows editors of the node's space, or any member of the grantee group, admin or not. Members can also list those grants. Inserting and updating grants is editor-only.
- **Recommended default:** (a). Removing a grant unshares another space's node for everyone in the group, which is the owner's call, and it matches the insert rule. Expected result: a non-editor member's delete is refused.

## SEC-04: Does removing a group's space access also end reads through that group's existing per-node grants?

- **Options**
  - (a) Yes. Table and storage reads require the same space access the views do.
  - (b) No. Per-node grants stand alone; space access only affects the views.
  - (c) Removing space access also deletes the group's grants for that space.
- **Code today**
  - The views need space access plus a grant. The table read rules (Concept, Content, Document, FileReference) and storage access accept a grant alone, and nothing deletes grants when space access is removed.
  - No app removes space access; only an editor of the space can. Some app paths read the tables directly, for example Obsidian's refresh reads Content, so they would still get rows.
- **Recommended default:** (a). Every reader then agrees with the views, and the grants survive if access is restored. Expected result: after removal, nothing of A's is readable by G's members through the views, the tables or storage. The explicit grant-removal control also ends reads.

## Not covered here

- Settled by the review: SRC-03 (the placeholder was chosen; the collision fallback is SRC-12) and TXT-08 (the heading-removal premise no longer holds).
- Decide cases at P2: DSC-09, TTL-07, SCH-06, UX-09.
- UX-06 (P2, high risk) also leaves one question open: whether the Obsidian import notice counts the Source that came along automatically.

## Problem

* Some MVP0 behavior may not be reliably automated in plugin runtime tests.
* Internal testers need a clear script with expected results.

## Scope

* The script is the push/pull test matrix: 175 cases in 17 areas, each with steps, an expected result, the directions it runs in (RR, RO, OR, OO; three-letter codes name the owner, contributor and consumer spaces), a method and the evidence a pass needs.
* It covers share, discover, import, refresh, relations, assets and access boundaries, for Roam to Obsidian, Obsidian to Roam, and each app to itself. Authorized paths and unauthorized paths (DSC, SEC) are both included.
* Known gaps are marked in each line below (21 cases). Cases that need a product decision say so and are listed under Open decisions (21).
* Isolated cases break or delete data on purpose and run only on throwaway spaces and a throwaway group. Access-control cases (SEC) and local-database cases run only against a local database, by an engineer.
* Failure reporting: capture the steps, actual result, spaces, accounts, logs and fixture state when the failure happens. A video comes later, when it helps explain the failure or a product question.
* Ratings in the matrix are predictions from reading the code, not results. Results belong to ENG-1883, one record per candidate run.

## Journeys

Run these four first on every candidate. They are the smoke checks.

- **J-RR** Full journey, Roam to Roam (P0; RR): Source comes along with the Evidence; title reads “[[EVD]] - … - [[@Source]]”; image re-hosted in graph B; once the Claim is imported the relation is pending, then accepted; Refresh updates the same page; deleted Claim reports it is no longer shared and the local copy stays.
- **J-RO** Full journey, Roam to Obsidian (P0; RO): File “EVD - … - @Source.md”; image downloaded into the vault; exactly one Evidence→Source relation; once the Claim is imported its relation is pending, then accepted; Refresh updates the same file; deleted Claim fails to refresh and the file stays.
- **J-OR** Full journey, Obsidian to Roam (P0; OR): Source comes along; title “[[EVD]] - … - [[@Source]]”; image embedded from graph B's storage; once the Claim is imported the relation is pending, then accepted; Refresh updates the same page; deleted Claim reports it is no longer shared.
- **J-OO** Full journey, Obsidian to Obsidian (P0; OO): Same as the Obsidian-to-Obsidian reference flow: files under import/<space>/, assets beside them, one Source relation, Refresh overwrites, deleted Claim fails to refresh.

## Cases by area

### Share and publish (PUB)

- **PUB-01** Publish one node from the page title (P0; RR, RO): Success toast. The node, its node type and the group grant are written; a group member in another space sees it.
- **PUB-02** Publish a note from Obsidian (P0; OR, OO): “Published successfully”; the button reads “Published (1)”; other spaces see the node.
- **PUB-03** Publish to two groups, then reopen (P1; RR, RO, OR, OO): Roam pre-checks both groups; Obsidian marks both “(shared)”. The G2-only space sees the node.
- **PUB-04** Uncheck a group that is already shared (P1; RR, RO): Needs a decision (see Open decisions).
- **PUB-05** Imported node offers no way to publish (Roam) (P0; RR, OR): No path publishes an imported node.
- **PUB-06** Imported note can't be published (Obsidian) (P1; RO, OO): Both are hidden.
- **PUB-07** Publish query results with mixed rows (P2; RR, RO): Only discourse nodes publish, and the toast gives a clear success and failure count.
- **PUB-08** Publish with suggestive mode off

````markdown
## Problem

* Some MVP0 behavior may not be reliably automated in plugin runtime tests.
* Internal testers need a clear script with expected results.

## Scope

* The script is the push/pull test matrix: 175 cases in 17 areas, each with steps, an expected result, the directions it runs in (RR, RO, OR, OO; three-letter codes name the owner, contributor and consumer spaces), a method and the evidence a pass needs.
* It covers share, discover, import, refresh, relations, assets and access boundaries, for Roam to Obsidian, Obsidian to Roam, and each app to itself. Authorized paths and unauthorized paths (DSC, SEC) are both included.
* Known gaps are marked in each line below (21 cases). Cases that need a product decision say so and are listed under Open decisions (21).
* Isolated cases break or delete data on purpose and run only on throwaway spaces and a throwaway group. Access-control cases (SEC) and local-database cases run only against a local database, by an engineer.
* Failure reporting: capture the steps, actual result, spaces, accounts, logs and fixture state when the failure happens. A video comes later, when it helps explain the failure or a product question.
* Ratings in the matrix are predictions from reading the code, not results. Results belong to ENG-1883, one record per candidate run.

## Journeys

Run these four first on every candidate. They are the smoke checks.

- **J-RR** Full journey, Roam to Roam (P0; RR): Source comes along with the Evidence; title reads “[[EVD]] - … - [[@Source]]”; image re-hosted in graph B; once the Claim is imported the relation is pending, then accepted; Refresh updates the same page; deleted Claim reports it is no longer shared and the local copy stays.
- **J-RO** Full journey, Roam to Obsidian (P0; RO): File “EVD - … - @Source.md”; image downloaded into the vault; exactly one Evidence→Source relation; once the Claim is imported its relation is pending, then accepted; Refresh updates the same file; deleted Claim fails to refresh and the file stays.
- **J-OR** Full journey, Obsidian to Roam (P0; OR): Source comes along; title “[[EVD]] - … - [[@Source]]”; image embedded from graph B's storage; once the Claim is imported the relation is pending, then accepted; Refresh updates the same page; deleted Claim reports it is no longer shared.
- **J-OO** Full journey, Obsidian to Obsidian (P0; OO): Same as the Obsidian-to-Obsidian reference flow: files under import/<space>/, assets beside them, one Source relation, Refresh overwrites, deleted Claim fails to refresh.

## Cases by area

### Share and publish (PUB)

- **PUB-01** Publish one node from the page title (P0; RR, RO): Success toast. The node, its node type and the group grant are written; a group member in another space sees it.
- **PUB-02** Publish a note from Obsidian (P0; OR, OO): “Published successfully”; the button reads “Published (1)”; other spaces see the node.
- **PUB-03** Publish to two groups, then reopen (P1; RR, RO, OR, OO): Roam pre-checks both groups; Obsidian marks both “(shared)”. The G2-only space sees the node.
- **PUB-04** Uncheck a group that is already shared (P1; RR, RO): Needs a decision (see Open decisions).
- **PUB-05** Imported node offers no way to publish (Roam) (P0; RR, OR): No path publishes an imported node.
- **PUB-06** Imported note can't be published (Obsidian) (P1; RO, OO): Both are hidden.
- **PUB-07** Publish query results with mixed rows (P2; RR, RO): Only discourse nodes publish, and the toast gives a clear success and failure count.
- **PUB-08** Publish with suggestive mode off

72	Both are unverified and high priority. Test only on an isolated local database, as an ordinary authenticated outsider with no membership in the target space or group. Keep privileged setup separate from the action under test, and include a permitted-member control. Keep the evidence local and restricted. If confirmed, file a private Linear issue, never a public GitHub issue or attachment.

74	**SEC-01: outsider grants itself access through the account functions.**
75	- **Invariant:** a caller with no SpaceAccess on space S cannot create or raise SpaceAccess on S for any account through `upsert_account_in_space`, `upsert_accounts_in_space` or `create_account_in_space`.
76	- **Where:** `packages/database/supabase/schemas/account.sql`.
77	  - `my_permissions_in_space` (228-237) returns `max(permissions)` over the caller's accounts, which is NULL for a non-member.
78	  - `upsert_account_in_space` (324-371) is SECURITY DEFINER with no membership check. It inserts SpaceAccess with `least(my_permissions_in_space(space_id_), COALESCE(permissions_, 'editor'))`. PostgreSQL's `LEAST` ignores NULL, so the value becomes the requested permission, `editor` by default.
79	  - The wrappers `upsert_accounts_in_space` (373-395) and `create_account_in_space` (397-410) call it.
80	  - Migration source: `migrations/20260213155959_upsert_user_permissions.sql`.
81	- **Precondition to confirm:** the grant goes to the `dg_account` of the PlatformAccount matching (`account_local_id`, S's platform). So escalation needs an `account_local_id` on S's platform whose `dg_account` is the caller's own auth uid.
82	- **What to observe:**
83	  - the RPC result
84	  - the SpaceAccess row
85	  - reads of S's Concept and Content, and writes to S's rows, as the caller afterwards
86	
87	**SEC-02: outsider joins through a group membership row.**
88	- **Invariant:** a caller can add a membership only for a group it administers, and `group_id` must be a group account. No insert can make another space's account uid part of the caller's `my_user_accounts()`.
89	- **Where:** `packages/database/supabase/schemas/account.sql`.
90	  - Table at 140-147: `admin` defaults to true.
91	  - `my_user_accounts` at 216-224 returns the caller's uid plus every `group_id` it is a member of.
92	  - `group_exists` at 257-263 is true only when any membership row has that `group_id`.
93	  - Insert policy at 586: `is_group_admin(group_id) OR NOT group_exists(group_id)`. There is no check on `member_id` or on the kind of account.
94	  - Migration source: `migrations/20260101183250_group_access.sql:62`.
95	- **Variants:**
96	  - (a) `group_id` is another space's anon uid. Co-member uids are visible through the group_membership select policy (580) and `my_pseudo_accounts` (461-477).
97	  - (b) Rejoin a group all of whose members have left.
98	- **What to observe:**
99	  - whether the insert succeeds
100	  - the resulting `my_user_accounts()`
101	  - reads and writes in the target space
102

104	- **SEC-03:** any member of a grantee group can delete that group's ResourceAccess rows (`content.sql:740`). This is a decision, not yet a bug.

## Access-control hypotheses

Both are unverified and high priority. Test only on an isolated local database, as an ordinary authenticated outsider with no membership in the target space or group. Keep privileged setup separate from the action under test, and include a permitted-member control. Keep the evidence local and restricted. If confirmed, file a private Linear issue, never a public GitHub issue or attachment.

**SEC-01: outsider grants itself access through the account functions.**
- **Invariant:** a caller with no SpaceAccess on space S cannot create or raise SpaceAccess on S for any account through `upsert_account_in_space`, `upsert_accounts_in_space` or `create_account_in_space`.
- **Where:** `packages/database/supabase/schemas/account.sql`.
  - `my_permissions_in_space` (228-237) returns `max(permissions)` over the caller's accounts, which is NULL for a non-member.
  - `upsert_account_in_space` (324-371) is SECURITY DEFINER with no membership check. It inserts SpaceAccess with `least(my_permissions_in_space(space_id_), COALESCE(permissions_, 'editor'))`. PostgreSQL's `LEAST` ignores NULL, so the value becomes the requested permission, `editor` by default.
  - The wrappers `upsert_accounts_in_space` (373-395) and `create_account_in_space` (397-410) call it.
  - Migration source: `migrations/20260213155959_upsert_user_permissions.sql`.
- **Precondition to confirm:** the grant goes to the `dg_account` of the PlatformAccount matching (`account_local_id`, S's platform). So escalation needs an `account_local_id` on S's platform whose `dg_account` is the caller's own auth uid. Also confirm the caller's effective execute privilege on each function (HR SEC-01).
- **What to observe:**
  - the RPC result
  - the SpaceAccess row
  - reads of S's Concept and Content, and writes to S's rows, as the caller afterwards

**SEC-02: outsider joins through a group membership row.**
- **Invariant:** a caller can add a membership only for a group it administers, and `group_id` must be a group account. No insert can make another space's account uid part of the caller's `my_user_accounts()`.
- **Where:** `packages/database/supabase/schemas/account.sql`.
  - Table at 140-147: `admin` defaults to true.
  - `my_user_accounts` at 216-224 returns the caller's uid plus every `group_id` it is a member of.
  - `group_exists` at 257-263 is true only when any membership row has that `group_id`.
  - Insert policy at 586: `is_group_admin(group_id) OR NOT group_exists(group_id)`. There is no check on `member_id` or on the kind of account.
  - Migration source: `migrations/20260101183250_group_access.sql:62`.
- **Variants:**
  - (a) `group_id` is another space's anon uid. Co-member uids are visible through the group_membership select policy (580) and `my_pseudo_accounts` (461-477).
  - (b) Rejoin a group all of whose members have left.
- **Control:** creating a legitimate group still works (HR SEC-02).
- **What to observe:**
  - whether the insert succeeds
  - the resulting `my_user_accounts()`
  - reads and writes in the target space

**Lower priority, also from the database reader:**
- **SEC-03:** any member of a grantee group can delete that group's ResourceAccess rows (`content.sql:740`). A decision, not yet a bug; see `matrix/decisions.md`.
- **SEC-04:** after SpaceAccess removal, reads still work through ResourceAccess on the tables and storage (`content.sql:726`, `assets.sql:83-94`). Now a decision; see `matrix/decisions.md`.
- **SEC-05:** storage insert and update check only the bucket, and importers don't compare downloaded bytes with the hash (`assets.sql:134-157`). Test overwriting a readable object separately from pre-seeding a new key.
- **SEC-06:** `create-space` upserts the Space name before checking the password (`packages/database/supabase/functions/create-space/index.ts:77-117`, privileged client at 267). Check the persisted row, not only the error.

Prepared by the matrix session (Claude) on 2026-09-25. This file acknowledges `HANDOFF-CODEX.md` and accepts its ownership split. The matrix session writes this file and everything under `matrix/`. It doesn't touch `runs/`, `builds/`, `reviews/` or `HANDOFF-CODEX.md`.

## Case schema

Each case in `cases.json` has these fields:

- `id`: stable across revisions.
- `area`: one of JRN, PUB, DSC, TXT, TTL, SRC, AST, UPD, DEL, REL, SCH, CNV, COL, RND, UX, SCL, SEC.
- `title`
- `dirs`: any of RR, RO, OR, OO, 3S (three spaces), DB (database).
- `steps`
- `expected`: the observable outcome, or "Not specified" for a product question.
- `src`: the ticket or document behind `expected`.
- `rating`:
  - `risk`: code reading suggests `expected` won't hold.
  - `decide`: needs a product decision.
  - `gap`: known or accepted for v0.
  - `pass`: expected to pass.
  - `unknown`
- `why`
- `ev`: code or PR references for the rating.
- `method`: `bash` (real-product bug bash), `db` (local database test) or `auto` (automated conversion test).
- `evidence`: what a pass records, `shot` (screenshot), `log` (assertion output or log) or `receipt` (written receipt). Failures always get the failure capture and, later, a video.
- `pri`: P0 to P2.
- `smoke`: set on the four journeys.
- `iso`: needs throwaway spaces.

Counts at this revision:

- 172 cases.
- Ratings: 43 risk, 22 decide, 21 gap, 56 pass, 30 unknown.
- Methods: 156 bash, 10 db, 6 auto.
- Journeys J-RR, J-RO, J-OR and J-OO are the smoke checks.

A rating is a code hypothesis, not a result. A `decide` row stays unresolved until an expected outcome is agreed.

## What the matrix session checked by hand

Everything else in `why` comes from the reader reports and cites code, but wasn't re-read by hand.

- **UPD-04.** `getImportedNodeUids` has no page restriction, so refresh-all also walks relation, schema and type blocks that carry `importedFrom` (`apps/roam/src/utils/importedSourceIdentity.ts:81-94`, `refreshAllImportedNodes.ts:13`).

  - Confirmed: at load, `initializeSupabaseSync` runs `cleanupOrphanedNodes` (`apps/obsidian/src/utils/syncDgNodesToSupabase.ts:1133-1149`), which builds the local set from `metadataCache.getFileCache(file)?.frontmatter` (`apps/obsidian/src/utils/getDiscourseNodes.ts:18-52`).

## Access-control hypotheses

Both are unverified and high priority. Test only on an isolated local database, as an ordinary authenticated outsider with no membership in the target space or group. Keep privileged setup separate from the action under test, and include a permitted-member control. Keep the evidence local and restricted. If confirmed, file a private Linear issue, never a public GitHub issue or attachment.

**SEC-01: outsider grants itself access through the account functions.**
- **Invariant:** a caller with no SpaceAccess on space S cannot create or raise SpaceAccess on S for any account through `upsert_account_in_space`, `upsert_accounts_in_space` or `create_account_in_space`.
- **Where:** `packages/database/supabase/schemas/account.sql`.
  - `my_permissions_in_space` (228-237) returns `max(permissions)` over the caller's accounts, which is NULL for a non-member.
  - `upsert_account_in_space` (324-371) is SECURITY DEFINER with no membership check. It inserts SpaceAccess with `least(my_permissions_in_space(space_id_), COALESCE(permissions_, 'editor'))`. PostgreSQL's `LEAST` ignores NULL, so the value becomes the requested permission, `editor` by default.
  - The wrappers `upsert_accounts_in_space` (373-395) and `create_account_in_space` (397-410) call it.
  - Migration source: `migrations/20260213155959_upsert_user_permissions.sql`.
- **Precondition to confirm:** the grant goes to the `dg_account` of the PlatformAccount matching (`account_local_id`, S's platform). So escalation needs an `account_local_id` on S's platform whose `dg_account` is the caller's own auth uid.
- **What to observe:**
  - the RPC result
  - the SpaceAccess row
  - reads of S's Concept and Content, and writes to S's rows, as the caller afterwards

**SEC-02: outsider joins through a group membership row.**
- **Invariant:** a caller can add a membership only for a group it administers, and `group_id` must be a group account. No insert can make another space's account uid part of the caller's `my_user_accounts()`.
- **Where:** `packages/database/supabase/schemas/account.sql`.
  - Table at 140-147: `admin` defaults to true.
  - `my_user_accounts` at 216-224 returns the caller's uid plus every `group_id` it is a member of.
  - `group_exists` at 257-263 is true only when any membership row has that `group_id`.
  - Insert policy at 586: `is_group_admin(group_id) OR NOT group_exists(group_id)`. There is no check on `member_id` or on the kind of account.
  - Migration source: `migrations/20260101183250_group_access.sql:62`.
- **Variants:**
  - (a) `group_id` is another space's anon uid. Co-member uids are visible through the group_membership select policy (580) and `my_pseudo_accounts` (461-477).
  - (b) Rejoin a group all of whose members have left.
- **What to observe:**
  - whether the insert succeeds
  - the resulting `my_user_accounts()`
  - reads and writes in the target space

**Lower priority, also from the database reader:**
- **SEC-03:** any member of a grantee group can delete that group's ResourceAccess rows (`content.sql:740`). This is a decision, not yet a bug.
- **SEC-04:** after SpaceAccess removal, reads still work through ResourceAccess on the tables and storage (`content.sql:726`, `assets.sql:83-94`).
- **SEC-05:** storage insert and update check only the bucket, and importers don't compare downloaded bytes with the hash (`assets.sql:134-157`).
- **SEC-06:** `create-space` upserts the Space name before checking the password (`packages/database/supabase/functions/create-space/index.ts:77-117`).

The page discloses unverified access-control holes with exact SQL function names, file lines, and trigger steps against a live production backend, and the handoff rules say that kind of evidence should stay restricted. I should suggest he either share with named people/org-only rather than a public link, or let me strip the sensitive SEC details so the rest is safe to circulate broadly — and I should clarify I wasn't worried about teammates seeing it, just the link leaking outside the team. I also want to flag that decisions.md exists locally and he may want an easier way to review it.

The simplest fix for "where do I read and decide" is just listing all 15 decision cases compactly right here in chat with my recommended default for each, then asking him to flag any he disagrees with rather than building some separate interactive page.

I could also mention adding a "Decisions" section to the matrix page so others can see them too. Then I'm pulling together the actual list from decisions.md — things like whether v0 supports unsharing a node (no, deletion is the workaround), whether to warn when a target group can't see an Evidence's Source (yes), what happens when a space leaves a group (nodes stay visible), how Obsidian links/tags map to Roam page references, and whether Refresh preserves block ids and local edits (no, it overwrites).

I'm continuing through the rest: duplicate node titles across spaces get refused on import with a clear message, renamed Roam nodes keep sharing their last matched version, linked non-note files like PDFs travel but embeds are a known gap, asset placement follows today's existing rule, there's no "newer version exists" notification for v0 since refresh-all covers it, and removed relations stay removed and are remembered going forward.

Obsidian needs a reject button for pending relation dismissals. For relations that already exist on both sides, Roam should match Obsidian's behavior by sharing at the next sync and arriving on refresh. If a source deletes a relation, pending copies get withdrawn while accepted ones stay. Only space editors -- not any group member -- can delete a group's grants, and removing a group's space access should end reads through existing grants since tables and storage follow the views.

I'm noting that several of these recommendations will require actual code changes across multiple areas -- locking, aliasing, messaging, and file handling.

content.text:
**Videos: no, I didn't make any.** None were in scope for this pass, for three reasons:
- My repros are unit tests, not the real apps, so there's nothing on screen to record.
- Codex owns the live apps and hasn't run the journeys yet.
- Your rule is that videos show a live failure and are made in a separate session.

Once Codex reproduces a failure in the real apps, that run's capture feeds a recording session.

**Why restrict: I said it badly.** Sharing the page with your team is fine. My concern is only the six access-control cases (SEC-01 to SEC-06). They describe suspected, unconfirmed holes in the live database's permission rules, with the exact functions and lines to try. Anyone holding a public link could try them against the real backend before they're checked or fixed. Two ways to share it safely:
1. Share it with named people or your org only, instead of "Anyone with the link".
2. I strip the SEC details from the page, leaving "engineers only, details kept locally", so the link can go anywhere.

I'd do option 2, since then you don't have to think about who ends up with the link. Want me to?

**The decisions** are in `/mnt/data/projects/dg-validation-eng-1883/matrix/decisions.md`. The page only lists them, without options. Here's each one with my recommendation. "Code change" means agreeing creates a ticket. "No" means agreeing only fixes what the test expects.

| # | Case | Question | My recommendation | Code change |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | PUB-04, DEL-03 | Can you stop sharing a node in v0? | No. Mark it a known gap; the way out is to delete the node. Roam should lock already-shared groups so they can't be unchecked. | Small |
| 2 | PUB-11 | Warn when publishing an Evidence whose Source the group can't see? | Yes, name the Source in the warning | Yes |
| 3 | DSC-06 | A space leaves a group: do its nodes stay visible and keep updating? | Yes, as today; document it | No |
| 4 | TXT-04 | Do Obsidian links and tags become Roam page links? | Yes, but convert `[[Other\|alias]]` to Roam's alias form | Small |
| 5 | TXT-06 | Must Refresh keep block ids and local edits on an imported Roam page? | No for v0; Refresh overwrites the page | No |
| 6 | TTL-11 | Two spaces' nodes with the same title in one Roam graph? | Refuse the second import as today, but name the space in the message | Small |
| 7 | TTL-15 | A Roam node renamed so it matches no type? | Keep sharing its last version; known gap | No |
| 8 | AST-06 | Do files an Obsidian note links to, without embedding, travel with it? | Yes, for PDFs and other non-note files | Yes |
| 9 | AST-08 | Where do imported assets land in Obsidian? | Keep today's rule | No |
| 10 | UPD-09 | Show that a newer version exists? | No for v0; use refresh-all | No |
| 11 | REL-05 | Does a relation you removed stay removed? | Yes. Obsidian also needs a reject button on pending relations. | Yes |
| 12 | REL-07, REL-08 | When does a relation added later between two already-shared nodes arrive? | Make Roam match Obsidian: shared at the next sync, arrives on Refresh | Yes |
| 13 | REL-09 | The source deletes a relation the destination has? | Pending copies go away; accepted copies stay | Yes |
| 14 | SEC-03 | Can any group member remove the group's access to another space's node? | No, only editors of the node's own space | Yes |
| 15 | SEC-04 | Does removing a group's access to a space also cut off reads through its per-node grants? | Yes | Yes |

To decide, reply here with something like "take the defaults except 8 and 12: keep today". I'll write the answers into the cases, rebuild the page and update the ENG-1881 text. If you'd like other people to see these too, I can add a Decisions section to the page.

# Qualified source finding: Obsidian native relation publication

Candidate: `b3796a70b526541014c92a40f685389060b862fe`  
Scope: bounded source reading plus one pure candidate unit assertion. No application, browser, Docker, database or network action occurred in this worker.

## Live observation supplied to this investigation

At 12:43:53, native Obsidian **Add Supports** created a relation with bare local `nodeInstanceId` endpoints, `created` but no `lastModified`, and later `publishedToGroupId`. At 12:46:35 its group had `ResourceAccess` for the relation, type and triple while the relation `Concept` instance was absent. A manual full sync at 12:47:13 later created the instance. That observation is live evidence; the source findings below do not replace it.

## What the candidate source establishes

1. **Bare endpoints and omitted `lastModified` are normal inputs.** `addRelationNoCheck` writes the IDs it receives, sets `created`, and does not set `lastModified` (`relationsStore.ts:145-164`). Conversion intentionally uses `(lastModified || created)` and looks up those bare IDs in `allNodesById` (`syncDgNodesToSupabase.ts:692-708`, `conceptConversion.ts:199-254`).

2. **A relation-only publication still builds the vault endpoint map.** `publishNewRelation` calls `syncAllNodesAndRelations(plugin, context, true)` before creating `ResourceAccess` (`publishNode.ts:81-149`). `relationsOnly` makes `changedNodeInstances` empty, but the sync still calls `collectDiscourseNodesFromVault` and passes `allNodes` to conversion (`syncDgNodesToSupabase.ts:480-521`). The converter builds `allNodesById` from that complete vault collection. Therefore a relation with the observed bare endpoints converts if both nodes are in the collected map and its type is accepted.

3. **The `missing:` console line is a batch-dependency diagnostic, not a failed endpoint-map lookup.** `orderConceptsByDependency` reports every reference absent from the current _upsert batch_, then still appends the relation to `ordered` and returns it to `upsert_concepts` (`conceptConversion.ts:262-335`, `syncDgNodesToSupabase.ts:710-735`). On a relations-only run, endpoint instances are deliberately absent from `nodesSince`; unchanged type/triple schemas can also be absent. Thus the manual-sync line containing both endpoint IDs and the relation type is expected from an otherwise convertible relation whose dependencies are already persisted. It cannot itself explain why the relation instance was absent.

4. **Resource grants do not prove the relation Concept existed.** `publishNewRelation` syncs first, then unconditionally upserts `ResourceAccess` for the relation/type/triple IDs if the endpoint files, publication groups and schema checks pass. There is no local check that the corresponding `Concept` row exists before those grants (`publishNode.ts:89-149`). The supplied grant/absent-instance observation is therefore a coherent state in this path.

## Remaining qualified possibilities

- The relation conversion filter excludes it if `created <= lastRelationsSync`, if it is imported, `tentative === false`, or its relation type is not accepted. The source does not expose which predicate applied to the 12:43 run.
- `relationInstanceToLocalConcept` returns `null` only if the relation type is missing or either endpoint is absent from `allNodesById`; this would log `Missing relationType id …` or `Cannot find the nodes`, not the supplied `missing:` dependency list.
- The relation-only sync could otherwise have completed and the later database observation may reflect timing or an unseen database/RPC outcome. Source reading cannot distinguish those explanations.

## Focused candidate check

`apps/obsidian/src/utils/__tests__/relationInstanceToLocalConcept.test.ts` passes. It calls the actual converter with the observed shape: no `lastModified`, bare endpoint IDs, and a vault map containing both nodes. It returns the relation Concept with those bare references. The subsequent dependency ordering reports the endpoint IDs and type as missing from a one-relation batch while retaining the relation in `ordered`.

```sh
pnpm exec vitest run --config vitest.config.mts src/utils/__tests__/relationInstanceToLocalConcept.test.ts
```

Result: 1 file, 1 test passed.

## Next live retest owned by the parent

For the native **Add Supports** flow, capture immediately before and after the internal relation-only sync: the relation's `created`, `lastModified`, `tentative`, `importedFromRid`, type acceptance, the `lastRelationsSync` query result, and the `upsert_concepts` payload/result. Keep the manual full sync as a separate control. This tests the filter/RPC path without conflating the expected dependency diagnostic with endpoint conversion or imported-relation cases.

Yes, several things are broken. Here they are in one place, most serious first. For context: I wrote the test list and code-level tests for six risky rows; Codex ran the real apps and the local database, and its second worker wrote code-level tests for nine more rows.

**Broken, seen in the real system (local database):**
- **SEC-02, security.** An ordinary signed-in outsider could join an empty group, then read and change a space they had no access to. Fix this first, on a private ticket.

**Broken in the candidate's code (tests run against the real code, not yet seen in the apps):**

| Case | What goes wrong | How bad |
| --- | --- | --- |
| DEL-04 | If Obsidian's `relations.json` is broken or missing, the next sync deletes all of that vault's relations from the database and still says "synced successfully". | Data loss |
| REL-13 | A relation published from Roam that points at an imported node is rejected, so other spaces never see it. Cross-space relations from Roam don't work. | Core feature broken |
| REL-15 | In Obsidian, an incoming relation to your own note shows on the other note but not on yours. | Core feature broken |
| REL-10 | One ambiguous relation type stops every relation in that import. | High |
| REL-18 | Roam republishes relations it imported as if they were your own. | Medium |
| REL-11 | Roam's query builder counts relations still pending review as real. | Medium |
| UPD-10 | After five failed syncs in a row, Roam stops syncing and tells no one. | Medium |
| UPD-04 | Roam's "Refresh all" reports each imported relation and type as failed, with no reason, for example "3 failed". | Misleading, no data harm |
| AST-04 | A PDF or video from Roam still points at Roam in Obsidian, not at the downloaded file. | Medium |
| UX-02 | The Roam import dialog stays on "Importing N of N" and can't be closed until relations finish. | Low |
| PUB-09 | A note you just converted in Obsidian can't be published until it syncs. | Low |
| AST-20 | File links inside code blocks get rewritten. | Low |

**Worked:** all four full journeys (Roam→Roam, Roam→Obsidian, Obsidian→Roam, Obsidian→Obsidian), after Codex fixed errors in its own test setup. They covered publishing, finding the node, importing it with its Source and image, importing and accepting a relation, refreshing after an edit, and a deleted source leaving the local copy intact.

**Still unclear:**
- **SEC-01** couldn't be judged. The function errored (PostgreSQL 42804) for the legitimate member as well as the outsider, so either the test called it wrong or the function is broken for everyone.
- **Obsidian relation timing:** once, a new Obsidian relation had its sharing grants before its database row existed, until a manual sync. It needs a clean retest.

**Not tested yet:** REL-13, REL-15 and PUB-05 in the real apps (Codex's next queue), and most of the other ~150 cases.

My suggested order: SEC-02, then DEL-04, then REL-13 and REL-15. I can draft bug tickets for these now, held as drafts until you approve them. SEC-02 would go on a private ticket. Want me to?

content.content:
**ENG-1985 Converters between the database and cross-app schemas.** Backlog; MAP.
- MG: only crossAppNode→content and crossAppNode→concept are needed now.

**ENG-2176 Escape regex metacharacters in format expressions.** Backlog.
- Only `[ ] ? . +` are escaped, so `Claim (draft) - {content}` never matches its own titles. Obsidian then publishes the full basename as `core_title`.
- DW: that format matches in both apps via one shared, tested helper, and formats without metacharacters are unchanged.

**ENG-2195 Normalize imported formats for Obsidian filenames.** Backlog.
- Problem: a Roam `[[CLM]] - {content}` format is stored raw, producing `[[CLM]] - sleep improves memory.md`.
- DW: store `CLM - {content}` instead. Formats containing `#`, `^`, `[`, `]` or `|` are normalized.
- MG marked ENG-2176 and ENG-2195 as possible duplicates.

**ENG-2207 Shared format resolver.** Backlog.
- DW: top-level `format` beats legacy `source_data.format` in both apps.

## No milestone

**ENG-2295 Show source details outside the Roam import table columns.** Triage.
- DW: agree the location and details, and let users inspect them while choosing nodes. The "Source app" column is not coming back.

**ENG-2232 Offer publishing the referenced Source with the Evidence.** Triage; post-v0 per MG.
- DW: the user can choose to publish both, the result names the Sources shared this way, and omit-and-warn stays available.
- Open question: is it a per-publish choice, a group setting, or the new default?

**ENG-2198 Reserved node type names (Page, Block, Any).** Backlog, Low.
- In v0, remote schemas with these names never resolve to local types and are never created, so "their nodes are skipped on import". The Post-V0 twin is ENG-2210.

**ENG-2261 Obsidian schema import conflict resolution.** Merged 09-22; Trang Doan; PR #1444; a different project (onboarding).
- This is the schema-file import modal ("Import discourse graph schema", step 3/3 "Resolve conflicts"). It is not the push-pull flow.
- DW:
  - Step 3 appears only when a selected item has a local match, and only differing fields are shown.
  - Checkboxes start unchecked. `Use theirs` and `Keep mine` apply per item.
  - `format` rows warn that existing titles are not rewritten.
  - The footer shows counts, e.g. `[Import 4 new · 2 merged]`.
  - `Back` discards the merge plan.

---

## Stated expected behaviors a tester can check

**Share and freshness**
- [ENG-2022, R→\*] With "Enable node sharing" on and suggestive mode off, the Publish tab, current-node command and page-title action work.
- [ENG-1851, R→\*] Page-title `Publish` opens Share Data on **Publish** with one node. Grants cover only the node and its schema, plus `SpaceAccess` `partial`.
- [ENG-1890, R→\*] The query-results dialog has `Send To`/`Export`/`Publish`, a group choice, a success/failure count, and skips or reports non-nodes.
- [ENG-1968, R→\*] Groups a node is already shared to appear pre-checked.
- [ENG-2022/ENG-2068, R→\*] A never-synced node publishes its schema, concept, title, full content and grant. A stale node updates on republish. A failed upsert grants nothing.
- [ENG-1852, R→\*] An edit to a shared node reaches remote on the next sync without re-sharing.
- [ENG-2294, O→R/R→R] An imported page has no publish button; refresh works; local pages still publish.
- [ENG-2141, R→\*] Evidence pushes its Source uid, or the origin RID for an imported Source. A missing Source publishes without the slot, with a warning that names it. Repeated pushes are identical.
- [ENG-2139, O→\*] Several Obsidian source relations resolve to the earliest-created one.
- [ENG-2153/ENG-2154, R→\*/O→\*] `core_title` holds the undecorated content, or the full title when there is no format or no match. It is stable across republish and sync.
- [ENG-2158/ENG-2175/ENG-2155] Schema rows carry `format`. Backfills report counts, are no-ops on re-run, and ENG-2175 is silent when idle.
- [ENG-1865, R→\*] A relation is published only when both endpoints are shared to the same group.
- [ENG-1870, R→\*] An image yields `FileReference` with `filepath` = URL and `filename` = upload name. The markdown is unchanged, an unfetchable asset is non-fatal, and an unchanged republish uploads nothing.
- [ENG-2280, R→O] An image added after sharing reaches the Obsidian vault after a sync and an import.
- [ENG-2230, O→\*] A bare-name link records the bare name in `filepath` and the vault path in `source_path`.

**Discovery and import**
- [ENG-1854] A group member sees the shared node; a non-member does not.
- [ENG-1855, O→R/R→R] The current dialog shows source app, space, title, source ID and modified time. Imported nodes are filtered or marked (changes under ENG-2296).
- [ENG-1859, O→R] Multi-select import reports imported/skipped/failed counts and survives partial failure.
- [ENG-1858/ENG-2098, O→R/R→R] Re-import updates the same page. R→R has no duplicate heading. An unsupported type gives an actionable error.
- [ENG-1856] The `discourse-graph.importedFrom` props survive a refresh.
- [ENG-2156, O→R/R→R] `CLM - my claim` becomes `[[CLM]] - my claim` and is recognized as that type. A type with no match is created once and then reused. An unchanged title doesn't change on refresh.
- [ENG-2142, O→R/R→R] A resolved Source gives `[[EVD]] - x - [[@Smith 2020]]`. A missing one keeps the verbatim title with a warning in the dialog or a warning-intent toast, and no placeholder.
- [ENG-2293, O→R/R→R] Importing Evidence alone also brings its accessible Source. An existing local Source is reused, and an inaccessible Source doesn't block.
- [ENG-1860/ENG-1861, O→R] Refresh overwrites local edits with no duplicates. Refresh-all reports refreshed/skipped/failed.
- [ENG-1857/ENG-2157/ENG-2292, R→O] The filename uses the local format. There is no duplicate H1, and refresh neither restores the H1 nor renames the file.
- [ENG-2298, R→O/O→O] A Roam space header shows no author; an Obsidian space shows its single author.
- [ENG-2140, R→O/O→O] Exactly one CurrentNode-to-Source relation, when that type exists. No duplicates on repeat.

**Relations**
- [ENG-1867/ENG-2215, O→R] A relation imports only when both endpoints exist locally. It is tentative, is not duplicated on re-import, and Obsidian endpoints resolve.
- [ENG-1869, O→R] The overlay shows tentative instances separately. Accept promotes without duplicating; a failure stays tentative with an error.
- [ENG-2131, O→R, pending merge] Settings → Grammar → Relations shows imported items separately with Accept/Delete. Delete is blocked when the schema is in use.

**Assets**
- [ENG-2219, O→R and R→R] Images render, served from the destination graph's own storage. A 404 asset leaves an intact body and a failure entry. Re-import doesn't re-upload.
- [ENG-2217, O→R] Media gets embed syntax, external URLs are untouched, and non-media links read `[report.docx](url)`.
- [ENG-2216/ENG-2218] A "Sync Asset Registry" block exists. Files are named `imported-<sha256>.<ext>`, with one upload per hash.
- [ENG-2289, R→R/O→R] pdf/audio/video/iframe/youtube embeds survive in both spellings.
- [ENG-2230, R→O] Roam assets get readable vault names, same-name assets coexist, and re-import is stable.
- [ENG-2288, pending merge] A failed sync copy is retried invisibly. The Export toast says "Publish again to retry."

## Known gaps and deferred items (not bugs if observed)

**Import dialog and UX**
- Discovery needs suggestive mode (ENG-2297).
- The import dialog is cluttered and uses the old labels (ENG-2296).
- There is no source-detail view (ENG-2295) and no Roam provenance indicators (ENG-1875).
- Obsidian status is unvalidated (ENG-1876).
- Failure reporting is not standardized, and degraded assets are not shown to users (ENG-1877).
- A zero-grant publish reads like success (ENG-1890 comment, no ticket).

**Source handling**
- Publish never shares the Source (ENG-2141; ENG-2232 post-v0).
- Imported-RID existence is not checked (ENG-2141).
- Evidence and Source edge cases (ENG-2142):
  - An unshared Source looks the same as "no source" because of RLS.
  - Evidence keeps its verbatim title until Refresh.
  - Renaming a Source cascades on Refresh.
  - Block-uid sources give a "not in this graph" warning.
  - A third placeholder keeps the title.
- Only one Source per node (ENG-2129, ENG-2139), and sources with `/` are excluded (ENG-2128).
- Obsidian never creates a missing CurrentNode-to-Source type (ENG-2140).

**Schemas and titles**
- Page/Block/Any schemas are skipped (ENG-2198).
- Raw Roam formats leak into Obsidian filenames (ENG-2195).
- Metacharacter formats never match (ENG-2176).
- Format precedence is implemented per app (ENG-2207). ENG-2208 and ENG-2209 are post-v0.
- `" - "` in content extracts the shortest match (ENG-2153), and the Obsidian extractor uses the first capture group (ENG-2154).
- Node types are created without review (ENG-2156), and schema matches are not recorded (ENG-1867).

**Relations**
- Re-import resets acceptance to tentative (ENG-1869).
- Type/triple review is unmerged (ENG-2131).
- Canvas: white arrows for lowercase labels (ENG-2317) and complement labels for same-type relations (ENG-2318).
- Endpoints are not auto-imported (ENG-1867).
- O-side relation validation is pending (ENG-1868; ENG-1866 post-v0).

**Assets**
- Assets don't refresh when upstream bytes change: a new file with a hash suffix appears and the old one is orphaned. A deleted asset causes a needless suffix (ENG-2230, ENG-1872).
- Copied files are never cleaned up (ENG-1872).
- Failed sync copies are not retried until ENG-2288 merges. Even then, ref'd or embedded assets are not retried, publish failures need a manual republish, and retries are unbounded (ENG-2288).
- Nodes shared before the asset stages are not backfilled (ENG-1870, ENG-2280).
- Bare-URL Roam attachments are not rewritten in Obsidian (ENG-1873).
- Obsidian MIME, size, access and fallback are not validated (ENG-1871).
- `fromMarkdown` limits (ENG-2289):
  - URLs with `[` or `]` break embeds.
  - Parentheses come back percent-encoded.
  - Already-damaged pages are not repaired.
- `{{query}}` and attribute lines import as literal text (ENG-2098).

**Other**

{"id":"P-DIS-166","uuid":"18c30753-b874-4691-9877-c5de444f66a2","icon":null,"color":"#bec2c8","name":"Push and pull nodes between Roam and Obsidian","summary":"Inter-graph: Roam/Obsidian","description":">>> ## Links

* [Roam Project](<https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/rOBMYfhKh>)
* [Scoping Doc](<https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/iC568HqDZ>)
* [Open Risks / Questions](<https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/TYHuKimqd>)

Follow the playbook for <project id="9e0670cc-3e1d-43db-bf20-f4118a5d050c" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/project/obsidian-within-lab-dg-collaboration-publish-and-import-9e316a1188b0">Obsidian within-lab DG collaboration (Publish & Import)</project>

>>>

>>> ## Goal

* Enable Roam and Obsidian to both act as source and destination for DB-backed Discourse Graph push-pull sync. MVP0 mirrors the existing Obsidian-to-Obsidian reference behavior: a source app shares one selected node to a group, shared persistence stores the node and required dependencies, and a destination app discovers, imports, and refreshes shared nodes from the other app. Assumes \[\[Project/Sharing group management\]\] is complete
* MVP0 / v0 is:
  * A Roam <-> Supabase <-> Obsidian flow, not a portable-package-first flow.
  * Single-node-share driven, matching the current Obsidian publish command. Import may still select multiple visible shared nodes.
  * Manual share/publish grants group access; already-shared source content stays fresh through each source app's existing local-to-remote sync behavior. Pull/import/refresh remains explicit/manual.
  * Group-targeted. The user chooses a group they belong to when sharing a node, after the separate group-sharing work is available.
  * Cross-app: Roam can source content for Obsidian, Obsidian can source content for Roam, and both apps can import from the other.
  * Markdown-first for content transport. \[\[\[\[ISS\]\] - v0 content model\]\] atJSON is the intended canonical content model, but it is not required for v0.
  * Built on existing Supabase auth, RLS, group access, content, concept, and file-reference tables where possible.

>>>

>>> ## Non-Goals

* MVP0 / v0 is not intended to solve:
  * Real-time bidirectional merge sync or collaborative conflict resolution.
  * Full atJSON storage, API negotiation, or app adapter rollout.
  * A complete portable package implementation.
  * New local persistence models for either app. Obsidian should keep markdown files, frontmatter, imported assets, and ; Roam should keep pages, blocks, and its existing relation representation.
  * Multi-node share as a single source operation. MVP0 share mirrors current Obsidian publish behavior: one node per share action.
  * Full recursive context export. MVP0 should preserve the selected node and required dependencies, not walk the whole reachable graph.
  * Direct sharing to individual users. MVP0 uses group sharing only.
  * Automatic remote-to-local polling or background pull into destination apps.
  * Explicit cross-schema translation, schema-equivalence UI, or automatic merging of incompatible local schemas.
  * Perfect preservation of every Roam or Obsidian formatting edge case.

>>>

>>> ## In-Scope Use Cases

>>> ### UC1: Source user shares one discourse node to a group

> * **Actor:** Roam or Obsidian user
> * **Trigger:** The user wants collaborators in another Roam graph or Obsidian vault to access one discourse node.
> * **Happy path**
>   * 1\. The user chooses a single discourse node to share.
>   * 2\. The user chooses one or many target group from the groups they belong to.
>   * 3\. The source app collects the selected node, required node schema, markdown content, origin identity, and any relation or asset dependencies valid to share under the Obsidian reference rules.
>   * 4\. The source app ensures the selected node and required dependency records are persisted through the normal local-to-remote sync contract.
>   * 5\. The source app grants access to the chosen group through shared persistence.
>   * 6\. Later local edits to the shared source node are propagated by the existing local-to-remote sync model; the user does not need to re-share unless the target group changes.
> * **Version:** MVP0

>>>

>>> ### UC2: Destination user discovers cross-app shared nodes

> * **Actor:** Roam or Obsidian user
> * **Trigger:** The user opens an import surface after being granted access to shared content from the other app.
> * **Happy path**
>   * 1\. The destination app queries visible shared resources.
>   * 2\. Nodes from the other app appear with source app, source space, title, source-local ID, and modified time.
>   * 3\. Already imported nodes are hidden or marked using stable origin identity.
> * **Version:** MVP0

>>>

>>> ### UC3: Obsidian user pulls Roam-origin nodes into a vault

> * **Actor:** Obsidian user
> * **Trigger:** The user selects one or more Roam-origin nodes from the import UI.
> * **Happy path**
>   * 1\. The Obsidian plugin fetches selected content, schemas, relation data, and resolvable asset references.
>   * 2\. The plugin materializes each Roam node as a markdown file under an import folder, with mapped , stable , and frontmatter.
>   * 3\. The plugin imports relations where both endpoints resolve locally, then reports import successes and failures.
> * **Version:** MVP0

>>>

>>> ### UC4: Roam user pulls Obsidian-origin nodes into a graph

> * **Actor:** Roam user
> * **Trigger:** The user selects one or more Obsidian-origin nodes from the Roam import surface.
> * **Happy path**
>   * 1\. The Roam extension fetches selected content, schemas, relation data, and resolvable asset references.
>   * 2\. The extension materializes each Obsidian node into Roam using the v0 markdown payload and Roam's markdown import/from-markdown capability.
>     * And changes to existing nodes are overwritten
>   * 3\. The extension stores stable origin identity so the imported node can be recognized and refreshed later.
> * **Version:** MVP0

>>>

>>> ### UC5: Destination user refreshes an imported cross-app node

> * **Actor:** Roam or Obsidian user
> * **Trigger:** An imported node has changed upstream and the destination user explicitly asks for the latest shared version.
> * **Happy path**
>   * 1\. The destination app identifies the source app, source space, and source-local node ID from stored origin identity.
>   * 2\. The destination app fetches the latest shared markdown content and metadata.
>   * 3\. The destination app updates the existing imported node without creating a duplicate and refreshes source timestamps.
>   * Any changes to the imported node are overwritten.
> * **Version:** MVP0

>>>

>>> ### UC6: Relation between separately shared nodes is preserved

> * **Actor:** Roam or Obsidian user
> * **Trigger:** The source user shares a discourse node that has a stored discourse relation to another node already shared to the same group.
> * **Happy path**
>   * 1\. The source app confirms both relation endpoints are shared to the same group.
>   * 2\. The source app writes the relation type schema and relation instance into shared persistence using the same semantic shape Obsidian imports today.
>   * 3\. The destination app maps or creates the local relation type and materializes the relation if both endpoints resolve locally.
>   * 4\. The destination app imports cross-app relation instances as tentative/unaccepted by default.
>   * 5\. Roam stores tentative relation state on the stored/reified relation record
>   * 6\. Tentative Roam relations are shown or discoverable separately from accepted local relations.
>   * 7\. A Roam user can accept or remove a tentative relation. Acceptance promotes it to the normal local relation set.
> * **Version:** MVP0

>>>

>>> ### UC7: Markdown content is later replaced by canonical atJSON

> * **Actor:** Engineer
> * **Trigger:** MVP0 is working and the team is ready to improve cross-app content fidelity.
> * **Happy path**
>   * 1\. Roam and Obsidian adapters convert app-native content into a DG-owned atJSON-compatible document.
>   * 2\. Destination adapters render that canonical document into the destination app's native local representation.
>   * 3\. The same canonical content can later render to Roam, Obsidian
> * **Version:** v1

I'm cross-checking my proposed decisions against the project's stated use cases and non-goals—like how local edits propagate without re-sharing, imported nodes get hidden or marked, and refreshes explicitly overwrite changes to imported nodes—to make sure nothing I'm proposing contradicts the defined scope.

I'm now working through each of the 15 decisions individually: for instance, the unshare feature isn't addressed in any UC so it seems reasonably out of v0 scope by omission, while the missing-Source-publishing suggestion appears to already be tracked as a deferred post-v0 ticket.

For decision 2 on Evidence-Source publishing, I'm distinguishing between a Source being entirely absent (which v0 already handles by omitting the slot and warning) versus a Source existing but not being shared with the group, which remains an open, narrower question. Decision 3 on leaving a group falls outside scope since it belongs to a separate group management project, and decision 4 on link/tag preservation aligns with the documented non-goal around formatting fidelity, deferred to a later markdown fidelity milestone.

Moving on, decision 5 on refreshing block IDs is settled since the imported node gets overwritten on updates, consistent with not preserving IDs. Decision 6 on duplicate titles is also settled—it refuses with a message while deeper collision UX stays out of scope. Decision 7 on renaming outside the expected format has no documentation, so it stays open, and I'm now checking decision 8 on linked files against the Obsidian asset validation work.

Location follows the existing Obsidian reference flow, settled. For newer-version updates, UC5 requires explicit refresh rather than background polling, and ENG-1875/ENG-1876 covering provenance indicators fall under the Internal validation milestone, meaning they're in v0 scope — I should check both tickets. Then for removed relations reappearing, UC6 step 7 lets a Roam user accept or remove a tentative match.

For relation sharing timing, UC6 shows it happens at share time, and ENG-1852 explicitly puts relation/asset freshness out of scope for v0 — so I'm settling on keeping this documented as out of scope, since neither refresh nor import flows currently handle relation freshness.

Looking at what's left, relation deletion upstream (REL-09) and the security items (SEC-03/04) fall outside this project's scope entirely, belonging instead to security policy or group management. That narrows the genuinely open items down to PUB-04/DEL-03, TTL-15, AST-06, and a couple of REL items still needing verification against ENG-1864.

I'm now cross-checking confirmed breakages against existing tickets: REL-13's cross-space relation issue doesn't map cleanly to ENG-2202 or the Roam-origin validation tickets since those are backlog validation items rather than fixes, and neither UPD-04 nor DEL-04 have dedicated tickets. ENG-1877, covering actionable failure reporting across Roam operations, seems to partially address the UPD gap.

Then I map REL-11 to a Codex finding on ENG-1867, tentatively link ENG-2296 and ENG-2297 to UX-02 and DSC-08, and note ENG-1875/1876 relate to provenance indicators. To verify these mappings, I'm pulling up the full descriptions for ENG-1864, ENG-1875, ENG-1876, and ENG-1877 in parallel.

The project description already answers several open questions—UC4/UC5 confirm imported node changes get overwritten, and the Non-Goals rule out background pull and perfect formatting fidelity. I'll now review four relevant tickets in the Internal validation milestone before mapping anything.

{"id":"ENG-1864","uuid":"ca579c26-4be5-4a26-9cfe-bd5375ecdb5a","title":"Define cross-app asset reference contract","description":"## Problem

* Roam and Obsidian need a shared asset reference shape for markdown import and link preservation.
* MVP0 must handle downloadable assets and URL-only fallbacks without blocking node sharing.

## Solution

* Define the reference shape: the token exactly as the node's content expresses it, the content hash, and an optional original name. Nothing else.
* Add Roam-origin and Obsidian-origin asset fixtures tied to shared node markdown, including a node whose content carries a token with no stored asset behind it.
* Support the missing, oversized, unsupported and no-row behaviors. These are specified as scenarios in the change's `cross-app-assets` spec; the work here is to make the shape carry them, not to restate them.

## Done When

* Shared asset reference payloads are documented or typed.
* Fixtures cover a stored asset and a node whose content carries a token with no stored asset behind it. The second is a content fixture rather than a reference fixture: `filehash` is `NOT NULL`, so an asset whose bytes were never stored has no row at all.
* Follow-up asset tickets can reference this contract without redefining payload shape.

## Out of Scope

* Uploading or downloading asset bytes.
* Markdown link rewriting in either app.
* Asset refresh behavior beyond metadata shape.

## Notes

* Functional requirements: [F10: Source asset publication](<https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/D-7HqQmKp>), [F11: Destination asset import and link rewrite](<https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/j3AqDVwfU>).
* Depends on [ENG-1847](<https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1847/define-shared-cross-app-node-content-contract>).
* Keep the contract source-neutral; app-specific asset handling belongs in implementation tickets.
* Two items from the original solution were designed out. `accessScope` was dropped because row-level security on the referencing node already determines read access, so a per-asset field would duplicate it more weakly ([Decision 7](<https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/xlPuc0A6E>)). Stored MIME type and size were dropped because no consumer reads them, and both are available from storage metadata when needed ([Decision 1](<https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/GQtp4l7g1>)).
* `filename` was added for the opposite reason to the fields above. It is the one piece a destination cannot derive for itself: without it an importer would have to recognise a Firebase URL and read Roam's own custom metadata, which is provenance detection in the consumer ([Decision 8](<https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/kd6Wpn_VF>)). The column itself is added by <issue id="bf853951-4407-4c8f-b22a-95e32c9f14ea" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2229/add-a-filename-column-to-filereference">ENG-2229</issue>.
* `CrossAppNode.assets` is defined here but has no runtime producer yet. `dbToCrossAppConverters` has no `CrossAppNode` converter — reads still go through the historical `SharedNode`. When that converter is written it should run the `my_file_references` query and populate `assets`. Until then importers query the view directly, and nothing should be wired to the field.
* **Proposed scope expansion: per-direction asset size caps.** Proposal only — `Done When` is deliberately left unchanged until this is accepted. The change itself is in commit `9e12a8f66400d99e0555556e4a35a5a93e5d9d16`.
  * **Need**
    * Engineers implementing <issue id="d002b2b0-a243-427d-9395-1ff708a953a5" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1870/copy-roam-origin-assets-into-supabase-on-publish">ENG-1870</issue> (publish) and <issue id="5613bacf-7236-4953-be21-e3e909d0a857" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2218/copy-one-asset-from-supabase-into-roam-storage">ENG-2218</issue> (import) each need to know what "too large" means before either can skip anything, and nothing currently defines it. Users are affected downstream: an oversized asset should degrade visibly rather than fail its node.
    * Evidence: the `cross-app-assets` spec carries the scenario "Asset exceeds the configured size limit", which has no referent without a number; the design's risk register records that both directions need an explicit cap and that neither may inherit one; and Obsidian's publisher enforces a bare `6 * 1024 * 1024` with no name (`syncDgNodesToSupabase.ts`).
  * **Fit and urgency**
    * Addresses a need the Solution above already names — it lists "missing, oversized, unsupported and no-row behaviors" among what the shape must carry. Defining the term is contract work; enforcing it is implementation work.
    * Relevant well within six months: <issue id="d002b2b0-a243-427d-9395-1ff708a953a5" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1870/copy-roam-origin-assets-into-supabase-on-publish">ENG-1870</issue> and <issue id="5613bacf-7236-4953-be21-e3e909d0a857" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2218/copy-one-asset-from-supabase-into-roam-storage">ENG-2218</issue> are in the current cycle and both read a cap.
    * Why now: whichever of those two ships first would pick the number and the second would inherit it — exactly the inheritance Decision 9 forbids, reintroduced by the ticket split rather than by anyone deciding it. The two caps are also deliberately paired, same value today but different rationale and expected to diverge; split across two PRs under different reviewers, the reason there are two constants rather than one is the part that gets lost.
  * **Triage**
    * Clear enough to implement, and small: two named constants, one predicate, one test, one call-site swap. A separate ticket was considered and rejected — its only consumers are this ticket's own follow-ups, and it defines contract vocabulary rather than app behavior.
    * Outcome: Ready for engineering ticket — folded into this ticket rather than cut separately.
    * Reason: shared vocabulary in `packages/database`, consumed by both directions and both apps, like `CrossAppAsset` itself. Recorded as Decision 9 in the change's design.
  * **If accepted**
    * `Done When` gains: Each transfer direction has its own named size cap, and an asset at or above it is skipped and reported rather than failing the node.

* Roam users need visible status for nodes that are shared or imported.
* Provenance details are currently not surfaced consistently near the node title.

## Solution

* Add Roam title-area indicators for shared source nodes and imported nodes.
* Surface published groups, last synced time, source app, source space, source title/local ID, and last refreshed/source-modified time where available.
* Reuse existing title-addition patterns where practical.

## Done When

* Shared Roam source nodes show a visible shared-state indicator.
* Imported Roam nodes show a visible imported-state indicator with source provenance.
* The indicators do not replace stored source identity metadata.

## Out of Scope

* Implementing share, import, or refresh behavior.
* Broader Obsidian status UX.
* Relation acceptance UI.

## Notes

* Functional requirement: [F14: UX status and provenance](<https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/7DN5ZOkhd>).
* Depends on [ENG-1851](<https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1851/add-roam-single-node-share-action>), [ENG-1856](<https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1856/store-source-identity-metadata-for-roam-imported-nodes>), and [ENG-1860](<https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1860/add-roam-manual-refresh-for-imported-nodes>).
